info.title: lemlist API
info.description:
Welcome to the lemlist Developer Documentation.

lemlist is very customizable and open. You'll find on this page all the API and integration you can do with lemlist.

# Rate Limit

lemlist's API rate limits requests in order to prevent abuse and overload of our services.  
Rate limits are applied on all routes and per API key performing the request.  
The rate limits are **20** requests per **2** seconds.  
The response provides any information you may need about it:

| Header | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Retry-After | The number of seconds in which you can retry |
| X-RateLimit-Limit | The maximum requests in that time |
| X-RateLimit-Remaining | The number of remaining requests you can make |
| X-RateLimit-Reset | The date when the rate limit will reset |

_Example of values for the rate limit headers_

``` json
{
    "Retry-After": 2,
    "X-RateLimit-Limit": 20,
    "X-RateLimit-Remaining": 7,
    "X-RateLimit-Reset" : "Tue Feb 16 2021 09:02:42 GMT+0100 (Central European Standard Time)"
}

 ```

# Definitions

## Team

A team is the entity of lemlist that can handle users and billing.

## Credits

Credits are the coins a team uses to enrich emails, LinkedIn URLs, etc. via the enrich route. Each enrichment feature needs a certain amount of credits to run.

## User

You use a user account to connect to lemlist and send messages via the connected emails or LinkedIn account.

## Campaign

A campaign is the entity to automate outreach. A campaign has multiple sequences composed of steps.

## Lead

A lead is a person that you try to contact via a campaign.

## Activity

An activity is the history of all the steps.

## Unsubscribe

An unsubscribe occurs when a person decides they don't want to receive emails from you anymore.

# Authentication

All API routes use the dedicated subdomain `api.lemlist.com`.

lemlist uses API keys to allow access to the API. You can get your lemlist API key at our [integration page](https://app.lemlist.com/settings/integrations).

You need to add the `Authorization` header using the `Basic` authentication type. `login:password` **where the login is always empty and the password is the API key**.

⚠️ **Don't forget to add the semicolon (**`:`**) before your API key in curl command.**

> To authorize, use this code: 
  

``` shell
curl https://api.lemlist.com/api/team \
  --user ":YourApiKey"

 ```

**Make sure to replace** **`YourApiKey`** **with your API key.**

# Give feedback

If you want to report a bug, ask for data, or share with us a use case, please fill this [form](https://lemlist.typeform.com/to/mfVlkyGf). It will help us centralize your needs!

tags.name: Enrichment Providers
tags.description:
The data providers lemlist can call to find an email or a phone.

Internal providers are paid with lemlist credits and always available. External providers run on your own account: connect one by saving its API key, and it becomes available to your waterfalls. `GET /enrichments/providers` is the catalog of provider ids accepted by the waterfall endpoints.

tags.name: Enrichment Waterfalls
tags.description:
Control which data providers lemlist calls when enriching a contact, and in which order.

A waterfall is an ordered list of providers for one enrichment `type` (`email` or `phone`). Providers are tried one after the other until one returns a result.

Every team has exactly one default waterfall per type (`isDefault: true`). While its `editor` is `lemlist` it follows the lemlist behaviour: providers you connected with your own API key are tried first, then internal providers in a random order. Once a team member edits its provider list, `editor` becomes that user's id and the list is followed as is; resetting it hands it back to `lemlist`.

Custom waterfalls (`isDefault: false`) carry `conditions` on the contact being enriched, keyed by contact property; every key present must match. When a contact is enriched, lemlist runs a single waterfall: the custom waterfall of the requested type whose conditions match the contact, or the default waterfall when none does. If several match, the one with the most condition keys wins, then the most recently updated. Only that waterfall runs; when it finds nothing, the enrichment ends without falling back to another one.

SelfRecoveryConfig.description: Account-level self-recovery configuration. Self-recovery watches the monitored signals and, when authorized, automatically runs recovery actions on degraded mailboxes.

teamId.description: ID of the team that owns the config.

enabled.description: Whether self-recovery is active for the account.

monitoredSignals.description: Signals self-recovery watches. `inboxPlacement` requires the placement test to be active.

authorizedActions.description: Strategies self-recovery may execute automatically. Only `fixDns` and `recover` can be authorized; `provision`, `replace` and `listHygiene` are diagnosis-only and rejected here.

digestFrequency.description: How often team admins get the recovery summary email: `daily`, or `weekly` on Mondays. Sent at 8am in the team timezone, only when self-recovery opened a case. Absent on configs created before this setting existed, which get the `daily` digest.

createdBy.description: ID of the user who created the config.

SelfRecoveryCase.description: A self-recovery incident case, opened when a monitored asset degrades. Append-only: one entry per trigger.

teamId.description: ID of the team that owns the case.

assetId.description: ID of the affected asset (a mailbox, prefixed with `usm_`).

assetLabel.description: Human-readable label for the asset (usually the mailbox email).

status.description: `recommended` when nothing ran (no authorized + wired action); `executed` when at least one recommendation was applied.

recommendations.description: Ordered list of recommended fixes (primary first).

lastDiagnosisKey.description: Internal key used to dedup identical diagnoses across ticks.

SelfRecoveryRecommendation.description: A single recommended fix produced by the diagnosis. A case can carry several.

rootCause.description: Diagnosed root cause of the degradation.

action.description: Concrete asset-level action the strategy executes.

explanationCode.description: Stable code for the explanation text, resolved client-side.

explanationVars.description: Ordered substitutions for the explanation text.

contributingSignals.description: Signals that contributed to this recommendation.

executionStatus.description: Automatic-execution outcome. Absent on pre-execution entries.

previousEmailsLimit.description: recover only: the daily sending limit before the volume cooldown.

LeadV2.description: A lead as the v2 endpoints return it: GET /leads/{email}, GET /leads with `version=v2`, and the `lead` nested in GET /activities with `version=v2`. `createdAt` is the date the lead was added to its campaign.

createdAt.description: When the lead was added to the campaign

state.description: Current state of the lead (e.g., scanned, contacted)

personalized.description: Whether the lead has personalized content

source.description: Source of the lead (e.g., api, csv)

variables.description: Custom variables associated with the lead

id.description: Campaign ID

CrmIdLinkErrorEnvelope.description: Error envelope of a refused `crmId` (closed beta) on the contact and company upserts. The extra fields name what to send instead.

code.description: Machine-readable error code, stable across releases.

message.description: Human-readable explanation.

conflictingRecord.description: With `CRM_ID_ALREADY_LINKED`: the lemlist record already linked to this CRM id.

contactId.description: The contact holding the id (contact upsert).

companyId.description: The company holding the id (company upsert).

survivorId.description: With `CRM_RECORD_MERGED`: the CRM record the sent one was merged into. Send this id instead.

convertedContactId.description: With `CRM_RECORD_CONVERTED`: the Salesforce Contact the Lead was converted into. Send this id instead.

ApiErrorEnvelope.description: Error envelope of the contact and company endpoints.

code.description: Machine-readable error code, stable across releases.

message.description: Human-readable explanation.

ApiErrorMessage.description: Error answered as a plain message by the contact and company endpoints.

ActivityType.description: A lemlist activity type. These are the exact values accepted by the `type` filter on GET /activities and returned as an activity's `type`. Mind the spelling: email types are plural (emailsSent), invites are linkedinInvite*.

LinkedinSubTypeCounts.description: A LinkedIn counter split by message sub-type. The three values sum to the aggregated counter of the same name on `perChannel.linkedin`. All three keys are always present, `0` when there is no matching activity.

CampaignPerChannelStats.description: Campaign counters split by channel. Only the channels requested through the `channels` parameter are returned; when `channels` is omitted, all five are present.

delivered.description: Emails sent that did not bounce.

linkedin.description: LinkedIn counters. `sent` covers message sends only — regular messages, InMails and voice notes. It excludes invitations and non-message actions such as profile visits, follows, likes, comments and endorsements.

sent.description: LinkedIn messages successfully sent, across the three sub-types.

delivered.description: Always equal to `sent`. LinkedIn has no delivery confirmation distinct from the send itself, so a LinkedIn delivery rate is always 100% and carries no information.

notDelivered.description: Send attempts that failed. Disjoint from `sent` — a failed attempt is never also counted as sent — so the share of attempts that failed is `notDelivered / (sent + notDelivered)`.

breakdown.description: `sent` and `notDelivered` split by message sub-type. Each trio sums to the counter of the same name above.

whatsapp.description: WhatsApp counters, messages and voice notes combined.

notDelivered.description: WhatsApp messages that failed to send.

others.description: Counters that belong to no messaging channel — API-driven and manual activities, fused to mirror the single entry of the in-app channel filter.

Team.description: The organization account that manages users and billing.

createdBy.description: User ID who created the team

createdAt.description: Date and time when the team was created

beta.description: Beta features enabled for the team

slackWebhook.description: Slack webhooks configured for the team

agency.description: Agency identifier if team is part of an agency

users.description: Team members with their basic details. Only returned when the request includes the `version=v2` query parameter.

Credits.description: Credits are the coins a team uses to enrich emails, LinkedIn URLs, etc. Each enrichment feature needs a certain amount of credits to run.

User.description: A team member account with connected email and/or LinkedIn sending capabilities.

role.description: User role in the team (admin, member, etc.)

linkedinUrl.description: The LinkedIn URL of the person

inviteLimit.description: Daily limit for LinkedIn connection invites

visitLimit.description: Daily limit for LinkedIn profile visits

inMailLimit.description: Daily limit for LinkedIn InMails (defaults to 5). The monthly InMail credits of the LinkedIn plan remain the hard cap

networkCheckLimit.description: Daily limit for LinkedIn network checks

withdrawInvitationLimit.description: Daily limit for LinkedIn invitation withdrawals

likeLastPostLimit.description: Daily limit for LinkedIn last-post likes

commentLastPostRetrieveLimit.description: Daily limit for LinkedIn last-post retrievals

commentLastPostSendLimit.description: Daily limit for LinkedIn last-post comments

inviteRampUp.description: How much the daily invitation limit grows each day until it reaches inviteLimit; null when the ramp-up is off

mailboxes.description: Email mailboxes connected to this user

Campaign.description: An automated outreach workflow containing sequences of steps.

emoji.description: Emoji shown next to the campaign name

timezone.description: IANA timezone the campaign schedule runs in (e.g. "Europe/Paris")

teamId.description: ID of the team that owns this campaign

errors.description: List of error messages if campaign has errors

id.description: Sender user ID

Lead.description: A contact added to a campaign for outreach. Not to be confused with a contact which is a record in lemlist, but not necessarily added to a campaign.

timezone.description: Lead's timezone in IANA format (e.g., Europe/Paris, America/New_York)

campaignId.description: Campaign ID the lead belongs to

campaignName.description: Campaign name the lead belongs to

Activity.description: A recorded action or event in a campaign sequence (email sent, opened, clicked, etc.).

stepId.description: Stable identifier of the sequence step that produced this activity. Present on every activity created from now on; older activities gain it progressively as historical records are backfilled, so treat it as optional when reading history.

sequenceStep.description: 0-based position of the step within the sequence. Still emitted on every activity, unchanged. Prefer `stepId` for a reference that survives steps being reordered.

totalSequenceStep.description: 0-based count of the sequence steps already delivered to this lead.

journeyDepth.description: 0-based depth of the step on the lead's own path: the step the lead reached before it, plus one. Skipped steps count; a step added to the sequence after the lead passed that point does not. Absent on activities recorded before the field shipped: read `totalSequenceStep` then.

contactId.description: Contact the activity relates to. Present on every activity, campaign or not.

leadEmail.description: Lead email as it was when the activity happened. Campaign activities only (absent when the activity has no `leadId`).

leadFirstName.description: Lead first name as it was when the activity happened. Campaign activities only, and only if the lead had the variable at that moment. For a name on every activity, read the current lead (`lead.variables.firstName` in v2) or the contact instead.

leadLastName.description: Lead last name as it was when the activity happened. Same scope as `leadFirstName`.

leadCompanyName.description: Lead company name as it was when the activity happened. Same scope as `leadFirstName`.

Unsubscribe.description: A record of someone opting out of receiving emails.

campaignId.description: Campaign ID from which the person unsubscribed

campaignName.description: Campaign name from which the person unsubscribed

UnsubscribedVariable.description: A variable (email, domain, LinkedIn URL, or phone number) that has been unsubscribed.

_id.description: Unique identifier for the unsubscribe entry

value.description: The unsubscribed variable (email, domain, LinkedIn URL, or phone number)

Enrich.description: An enrichment: one request to find an email or a phone number, verify an email or enrich a LinkedIn profile for one person. This is the shape `GET /enrich/{enrichId}` answers with; webhooks carry the same results under other key names (see the Webhooks section).

enrichmentStatus.description: Lifecycle state of the enrichment, not to be confused with `data.email.status`. Each state comes with its own HTTP status: `done` 200, `in-progress` 202, `failed` 400, `not-found` 404. A cancelled enrichment answers `done`.

input.description: The inputs the enrichment was started with, echoed back. Absent on `not-found`.

data.description: What the enrichment found, keyed by result. Empty unless `enrichmentStatus` is `done`. A key is present only for a requested workflow that produced a result. A `find_email` or `find_phone` that found nothing still has its key, with `notFound: true`. A requested workflow that ended without any result has no key and is listed in `failedWorkflows`.

email.description: Result of `find_email` and/or `verify`. Present only when one of them was requested and produced a result.
The address found by `find_email`. Absent when `notFound` is true or when only `verify` ran.

notFound.description: Set when `find_email` ran. True whenever no address is returned, including when the person opted out of enrichment: their address is never returned.

status.description: Deliverability of the address: the `verify` verdict, or the check `find_email` runs on the address it finds. Absent when no check resolved.

phone.description: Result of `find_phone`. Present only when it was requested and produced a result.
The phone number found. Absent when `notFound` is true.

additionalPhones.description: Other numbers returned by the provider, when it returned more than one.

notFound.description: True whenever no number is returned, including when the person opted out of enrichment: their number is never returned.

linkedin.description: Result of `linkedin_enrichment`: the LinkedIn profile as returned by the data source (identity, current company, `positionGroups`, …). Present only when it was requested and produced a result.

failedWorkflows.description: On `done`, the requested workflows that ended without any result; they have no key in `data`. A `find_email` or `find_phone` that found nothing is not listed: it answers `notFound: true` in `data`. A workflow lemlist runs on its own as a dependency of a requested one is never listed. Only present when not empty.

code.description: On `failed`, why the enrichment failed. An unknown or missing cause reads as `FAILED_TO_PROCESS`.

reason.description: On `failed`, a human-readable explanation of `code`, possibly translated to the language of the API user. Branch on `code`, never on `reason`.

error.description: On `failed`, the raw cause stored on the enrichment, absent when none was stored; prefer `code`. On `not-found`, `Enrichment not found`.

Task.description: A manual action assigned to a user to complete. Only the fields set on the task are returned.

type.description: Task type as stored, never `null`. Tasks created through the API use `email`, `manual`, `phone`, `linkedinSend` or `whatsappMessage`. Campaign tasks carry the type of their step (for example `linkedinInvite`, `whatsappVoiceNote` or `sms`), and reply and click tasks use `opportunityReplied` and `opportunityClicked`.

content.description: Task instruction, sent as `message` when the task is created or updated.

text.description: Text of the lead's LinkedIn reply, when it has one, on `opportunityReplied` tasks.

priority.description: `0` low, `1` medium, `2` high. Absent when the task has no priority.

dueDate.description: Due date. Tasks carry no creation date.

userId.description: ID of the assigned user, sent as `assignedTo`.

campaignId.description: Campaign ID. A task on a lead carries the campaign of that lead.

leadFirstName.description: First name of the lead or contact

leadLastName.description: Last name of the lead or contact

leadCompanyName.description: Company name of the lead or contact. On a company task, the name (or domain) of the company, the only field that identifies it: the response carries no `companyId`.

manual.description: `true` on tasks created by hand in lemlist or through the API, on campaign tasks whose step has its manual option on, and on out-of-office tasks. Absent otherwise, never `false`.

FieldRejection.description: A value lemlist refused to write on a Contact or Company, with the reason why. Surfaced under `fieldRejections[]` on those objects; filter a list endpoint to only flagged records via the `fieldRejectionReason` query param.

field.description: The record field the rejected value targeted (e.g. `emails`, `linkedinUrl`, `domain`).

reason.description: Why the value was rejected, prefixed by its origin — `enrichment_*` (raised while enriching) or `crm_sync_*` (raised during CRM sync). Same values accepted by the `fieldRejectionReason` query param.

source.description: Where the rejection came from — an enrichment source (`lemrich`) or a CRM provider (`hubspot`, `salesforce`, `pipedrive`).

conflictingRecordId.description: The lemlist record that already holds the value, when the rejection identifies one — use it to merge or remap before resolving the duplicate. Always a lemlist id (`ctc_…` for a contact, `cpn_…` for a company), never a CRM record id. Omitted otherwise.

Contact.description: A contact record in your CRM, as the lookups (`GET /contacts?idsOrEmails=`, `GET /contacts?crmIds=`, `GET /contacts/{idOrEmail}`) return it. Not to be confused with a lead which is a contact specifically added to a campaign.

teamId.description: Team identifier the contact belongs to

campaigns.description: List of campaigns the contact is associated with

ownerId.description: ID of the user who owns this contact

createdBy.description: ID of the user who created the contact

unsubscribed.description: Whether the contact is globally unsubscribed. When true, no outreach will be sent to this contact.

phonesStatuses.description: Verification status of each verified phone number.

phone.description: The phone number, as stored in `fields`

crmSync.description: CRM sync status for the contact, resolved against the team's active CRM provider (Hubspot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive). Only present when a CRM is connected and the contact has a record in it. `crmRecordId` maps a `crmIds` lookup back to the ids sent.

provider.description: Active CRM provider for the team.

crmRecordId.description: Identifier of the contact record on the CRM side. `null` when the lemlist contact has not been synced yet.

syncDisabled.description: When `true`, automatic sync is paused for this contact.

searching.description: `true` while a CRM search (Search & connect, Create in CRM) is queued or running for this contact, however long the queue takes. A search marked running more than 15 minutes ago with nothing left in the queue stalled: the read clears it and returns `false`.

notFoundAt.description: When the last CRM search found no matching record. `null` otherwise.

errors.description: List of recent sync errors. Empty when the contact is synced cleanly.

raisedAt.description: Timestamp when the error was last raised.

metadata.description: Extra context. For `UNIQUE_INDEX_ERROR_COMPANY`, contains `alreadyExistingCompanyId` — the lemlist company that already occupies the conflicting CRM record. Use it to remap contacts onto the right lemlist company before deleting the duplicate.

fieldRejections.description: Values lemlist refused to write on this contact, each with its reason. Empty when none. Filter the list endpoint to only flagged contacts via `GET /contacts?fieldRejectionReason=...`.

ContactListItem.description: A contact as the list (`GET /contacts` with filters or no parameter) returns it, with the main fields flattened. Properties with no value are omitted.

teamId.description: Team identifier the contact belongs to

ownerId.description: ID of the user who owns this contact

companyId.description: ID of the company the contact is attached to (`cpn_xxx`)

createdBy.description: ID of the user who created the contact

unsubscribed.description: Whether the contact is globally unsubscribed. When true, no outreach will be sent to this contact.

campaignCount.description: Number of campaigns the contact is in

crmSync.description: CRM sync status for the contact, resolved against the team's active CRM provider. Only present when a CRM is connected and the contact is linked to a record in it or was searched for in it. Read `searching` and `notFoundAt` to follow a Search & connect or Create in CRM.

provider.description: Active CRM provider for the team.

crmRecordId.description: Identifier of the contact record on the CRM side. `null` when the lemlist contact has not been synced yet.

syncDisabled.description: When `true`, automatic sync is paused for this contact.

searching.description: `true` while a CRM search (Search & connect, Create in CRM) is queued or running for this contact, however long the queue takes. A search marked running more than 15 minutes ago with nothing left in the queue stalled: the read clears it and returns `false`.

notFoundAt.description: When the last CRM search found no matching record. `null` otherwise.

errors.description: List of recent sync errors. Empty when the contact is synced cleanly.

raisedAt.description: Timestamp when the error was last raised.

metadata.description: Extra context. For `UNIQUE_INDEX_ERROR_COMPANY`, contains `alreadyExistingCompanyId` — the lemlist company that already occupies the conflicting CRM record. Use it to remap contacts onto the right lemlist company before deleting the duplicate.

fieldRejections.description: Values lemlist refused to write on this contact, each with its reason. Empty when none. Filter the list endpoint to only flagged contacts via `GET /contacts?fieldRejectionReason=...`.

Company.description: An organization record in your CRM.

teamId.description: Team the company belongs to. Returned by `GET /companies/{companyId}` and the `idsOrDomains` and `crmIds` lookups; the paginated list returns it only when requested with `fields`.

linkedinUrl.description: LinkedIn company page URL. Returned by `GET /companies/{companyId}` and the `idsOrDomains` and `crmIds` lookups; the paginated list returns it only when requested with `fields`.

linkedinUrlSalesNav.description: Sales Navigator company URL. Returned by `GET /companies/{companyId}` and the `idsOrDomains` and `crmIds` lookups; the paginated list returns it only when requested with `fields`.

fields.description: Key/value attributes of the company, standard and custom (e.g., name, picture, industry, location, size, foundedOn). These values are always under `fields`, never at the top level of the object.

createdBy.description: User ID who created the company

ownerId.description: User ID of the owner of the company

source.description: Origin of the company record, e.g. `api` when it was created through this API. Returned by `GET /companies/{companyId}` and the `idsOrDomains` and `crmIds` lookups, not by the paginated list.

fieldRejections.description: Values lemlist refused to write on this company, each with its reason. Empty when none. Filter the list endpoint to only flagged companies via `GET /companies?fieldRejectionReason=...`.

crmSync.description: CRM sync status for the company, resolved against the team's active CRM provider (Hubspot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive). Only present when a CRM is connected. Use this block to monitor sync state and resolve duplicates (e.g. via `GET /companies?crmSyncStatus=unique_index_error_company`).

provider.description: Active CRM provider for the team.

crmRecordId.description: Identifier of the company record on the CRM side. `null` when the lemlist company has not been synced yet.

syncDisabled.description: When `true`, automatic sync is paused for this company.

searching.description: `true` while a CRM search (Search & connect, Create in CRM) is queued or running for this company, however long the queue takes. A search marked running more than 15 minutes ago with nothing left in the queue stalled: the read clears it and returns `false`.

notFoundAt.description: When the last CRM search found no matching record. `null` otherwise.

errors.description: List of recent sync errors. Empty when the company is synced cleanly.

reason.description: Specific error reason. Matches the lowercase form accepted by the `crmSyncStatus` query param (e.g. `UNIQUE_INDEX_ERROR_COMPANY`, `PROPERTY_DOESNT_EXIST`, `REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING`).

raisedAt.description: Timestamp when the error was last raised.

metadata.description: Extra context. For `UNIQUE_INDEX_ERROR_COMPANY`, contains `alreadyExistingCompanyId` — the lemlist company that already occupies the conflicting CRM record. Use it to remap contacts onto the right lemlist company before deleting the duplicate.

DatabaseCompany.description: A company record from lemlist's People database.

Call.description: A call logged through `POST /calls`, as the calls API returns it.

_id.description: The call's activity id, which `PATCH /calls/{id}` and `DELETE /activities/{activityId}/recording-transcript` take.

externalId.description: Your own id of the call, as sent; `null` on a call another dialer made.

leadId.description: The lead the call attached to, when it belongs to a campaign.

taskId.description: The call task the call completed.

userId.description: The rep the call is attributed to.

from.description: The caller's number: the rep's line on an outbound call, the contact's on an inbound one.

callStatus.description: The key of the call status set on the call.

note.example: Asked for a demo next week.

phoneProvider.description: `api` for a call logged through this API; the dialer that made it otherwise (`twilio` for the lemlist dialer, `aircall`, `ringover`) on a call read back by `_id`.

provider.description: The dialer's name a call was logged with through this API (`provider`), lowercase; `null` when none was sent and on any other call.

hasRecording.description: True once the call has a recording in lemlist: a `recordingUrl` just sent is still on its way.

CallStatus.description: A call status (disposition) of the team, with the automations the team configured on it.

callAnswered.description: The status counts the call as answered in the reports.

callPositive.description: The status marks the lead as interested and stops its campaign.

callNegative.description: The status marks the lead as not interested.

pausesCampaigns.description: The status pauses campaigns for the lead or its company.

CompanyNote.description: A text note attached to a company record to store information.

teamId.description: Team ID that owns the company

userId.description: ID of the user who created the note

sendUserId.description: ID of the sending user if applicable

ContactNote.description: A text note attached to a contact record, as returned by `GET` and `POST /contacts/{idOrEmail}/notes`.

teamId.description: Team ID that owns the contact

userId.description: ID of the user who wrote the note

CrmLog.description: One operation lemlist ran with the team's connected CRM for a contact or a company, as returned by `GET /v2/crm/logs`.

doneAt.description: When lemlist finished the operation. Present on `done` logs and on logs aborted by a user or by a campaign move; absent on `pending` and `error` logs, and on other aborts.

crm.description: The CRM the operation ran against, e.g. `hubspot`, `salesforce`, `pipedrive`. A contact's or a company's history keeps the logs of a CRM the team has since left; the team history lists the connected CRM only.

direction.description: `lemlist_to_crm` for a write lemlist sent to the CRM, `crm_to_lemlist` for a change received from the CRM

method.description: Name of the operation, e.g. `contact_update`. `direction` tells a lemlist write from the CRM change it mirrors. Known values: `activity_create`, `activity_import`, `association_from_company`, `association_from_contact`, `association_remove`, `association_update`, `call_create`, `call_update`, `company_create`, `company_delete`, `company_merge`, `company_owner_update`, `company_restore`, `company_update`, `contact_create`, `contact_delete`, `contact_merge`, `contact_owner_update`, `contact_restore`, `contact_update`, `custom_activity_create`, `deal_create`, `email_message_create`, `event_create`, `experience_update`, `lead_status_update`, `linkedin_message_create`, `note_create`, `note_import`, `note_update`, `sms_message_create`, `task_complete`, `task_create`, `task_delete`, `task_import`, `task_update`, `whatsapp_message_create`. An operation lemlist has not named yet keeps its own identifier: filter with `category` rather than on this value.

label.description: Human-readable name of the operation, in English, e.g. `Contact update`. Equals `method` when the operation has no label.

category.description: Kind of record the operation acted on. Absent when the operation has no category.

state.description: `pending`: queued, not run yet. `done`: the CRM accepted it. `error`: the CRM refused it, see `error`. `aborted`: lemlist skipped it, `error.code` gives the reason.

contactId.description: The contact the operation is about (`ctc_xxx`). Present on contact rows and on the rows of a contact-company association.

companyId.description: The company the operation is about (`cpn_xxx`). Present on company rows and on the rows of a contact-company association.

crmObjectId.description: ID of the record in the CRM

updatedFields.description: Fields sent to or received from the CRM, with their values

error.description: Present on `error` rows, and on `aborted` rows where it carries the reason.

code.description: Stable error or abort code, e.g. `INVALID_EMAIL`

statusCode.description: HTTP status the CRM answered, when known

message.description: The CRM's own message, in English, untranslated. Its wording can change: rely on `code`.

Sequence.description: An ordered series of steps within a campaign.

Step.description: A single action in a sequence (email, LinkedIn message, delay, task, etc.).

customName.description: The step's own name, shown instead of its type label ("Email", "Call") wherever the app names the step. Absent when the step has none

abTest.description: A/B test state for this step. `true` while the test runs (leads are split between variant A and B); `"A"` or `"B"` once a winner is selected (all remaining leads receive the winning template); absent/false when there is no A/B test.

emailTemplateId.description: Email template ID of variant A

emailTemplateBId.description: Email template ID of variant B (present when an A/B test exists on the step)

sendToAnotherCampaignId.description: Applies to `sendToAnotherCampaign` steps only. Target campaign the lead is moved to.

leadAction.description: Applies to `sendToAnotherCampaign` steps only. What happens to the lead in the source campaign once it has been moved. Absent when the step carries no value, which behaves as `continue`.

ConditionBranch.description: One branch of a condition step. Addressed by `sequenceId` - the sub-sequence its leads walk - never by position. The fields describing what the branch tests depend on the step's condition; the ones that do not apply are absent.

sequenceId.description: The branch's sub-sequence id, and its address on every branch endpoint. Pass it to `POST /sequences/{sequenceId}/steps` to add steps inside the branch.

index.description: Execution rank among the non-fallback branches, starting at 0. The first branch whose test matches takes the lead. Absent on the Else branch, which always runs last.

fallback.description: `true` on the Else branch - the one that catches every lead no other branch matched. Absent on the others.

key.description: The condition the step tests. Every branch of a step shares it: a branch never carries a condition of its own.

name.description: The branch's display name, present only when someone has set one. lemlist labels the unnamed ones "Branch 1", "Branch 2", … and "Else"; those defaults are not stored and are not returned here.

delay.description: Length of the time window the condition waits on the lead's action, in days. Only on the lead-action conditions that store one.

delayType.description: How the condition waits: `within` branches once the window is over, `waitUntil` parks the lead until the action happens, with no time bound.

scoreComparator.description: `hasScore` only - how the lead's score is compared to `scoreThreshold`.

scoreThreshold.description: `hasScore` only - the score this branch tests against.

emailStatusFilter.description: `hasEmailAddress` only - the email statuses this branch matches.

callStatusFilter.description: `aircallDone` only - the call-status keys this branch matches.

customField.description: `customLeadInfo` only - the tested field, normalized: a lead variable reads back as `variables.<name>`, a contact field as `fields.<name>`, a company field as `company.<field>` (e.g. `company.name`), or as `variables.company<Field>` (e.g. `variables.companyName`) on a step that already tested it that way, which tests the same value. Every branch of the step tests the same field.

customOperator.description: `customLeadInfo` only - how the field is compared to the tested values.

customValues.description: `customLeadInfo` only - every value this branch tests; the branch matches when any of them does. Empty for the `empty` and `notEmpty` operators.

selector.description: The raw stored condition selector, as JSON. Returned only when none of the fields above could describe the branch.

stepType.description: The step type. Absent on a legacy email step.

sender.description: The forced sender of the step, in the shape of the request body. Absent when the step uses the sender strategy of the campaign.

userId.description: The team member who sends the step

type.description: The channel type of the step: `email` on an email step, `linkedin` on a LinkedIn step, `whatsapp` on a WhatsApp step, `phone` on an SMS step.

id.description: The account to send from: the mailbox id, the WhatsApp account id, or the phone number. On LinkedIn, the user id. Without `id`, the first healthy account of the type.

alias.description: Email only, with an `id`: the alias address of the mailbox to send from.

StepSender.description: The forced sender of a step.

SenderPoolChange.description: The channel types that a step change enables or disables in the sender pool. A type can be in both lists when one account of the type enters the pool and another leaves it. It does not tell whether each sender has an account of the type: read the diagnostics with Get Campaign Senders.

enabledChannelTypes.description: The channel types with an account that enters the pool, in alphabetical order

disabledChannelTypes.description: The channel types with an account that leaves the pool, in alphabetical order

SenderPool.description: The sender pool of a campaign, as the campaign editor shows it.

espMatching.description: `true` when a lead gets a mailbox of the same provider as its address, when the pool has one.

readOnly.description: `true` for a dynamic sender strategy: the leads select the senders.

channels.description: The enabled channels. Remove `label`, `esp` and `diagnostics` to get a valid `channels` entry of the request bodies.

id.description: The mailbox id, the WhatsApp account id, the phone number, or the user id for LinkedIn.

alias.description: Email only: the address the mailbox sends as.

esp.description: Email only: the provider of the mailbox.

diagnostics.description: The problems that block or limit the sending. See [Get Campaign Senders](/api-reference/endpoints/senders/get-campaign-senders#diagnostics).
The problems that block or limit the sending. See [Get Campaign Senders](/api-reference/endpoints/senders/get-campaign-senders#diagnostics).
The problems of the whole pool, for example no account of a required channel type in the team.

SenderDiagnostic.description: One health problem of a sender, a channel or the whole pool.

scope.description: What the problem is about: one channel, one sender, one step or the whole pool.

type.description: `error` blocks the sending. `warning` and `info` do not.

message.description: More details, for example the error of a mailbox.

channelType.description: The channel type of the problem. Absent when the problem is not about one channel type.

SenderChannelInput.description: One channel to enable on a sender.

type.description: The channel type. At least one step of the campaign must use it.

id.description: The account to enable: the mailbox id, the WhatsApp account id or the phone number. Omit it for `linkedin`. Without `id`, every healthy account of the type, or every account of the type when none is healthy.

alias.description: Email only, with an `id`: the alias address of the mailbox to send as.

channels.description: The channels to enable. Without `channels`, the sender gets the channel types that the campaign steps use, healthy accounts first, as the campaign editor does.

SenderList.description: The team members who can send, with their channels.

senderStrategy.description: With `campaignId` only. The sender strategy of the campaign.

requiredChannelTypes.description: With `campaignId` only. The channel types that the campaign steps use. Only these types can be enabled in the pool.

inPool.description: With `campaignId` only. `true` when the sender is in the pool of the campaign.

id.description: The mailbox id, the WhatsApp account id, the phone number, or the user id for LinkedIn.

aliases.description: Email only: the alias addresses of the mailbox.

esp.description: Email only: the provider of the mailbox.

inPool.description: With `campaignId` only. `true` when the pool enables the channel.

diagnostics.description: The problems that block or limit the sending. See [Get Campaign Senders](/api-reference/endpoints/senders/get-campaign-senders#diagnostics).
The problems that block or limit the sending. See [Get Campaign Senders](/api-reference/endpoints/senders/get-campaign-senders#diagnostics).

Schedule.description: Sending time windows defining when campaigns can send messages (days and hours).

public.description: Whether the schedule is available as a template for other users

teamId.description: Unique identifier of the team that owns this schedule

createdBy.description: Unique identifier of the user who created this schedule

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the schedule was created

deletedAt.description: Timestamp when the schedule was deleted (only present if deleted)

deletedBy.description: Unique identifier of the user who deleted this schedule (only present if deleted)

Webhook.description: Webhooks send real-time HTTP notifications upon campaign events (opens, clicks, replies, etc.).

type.description: Event type to listen for. Events are grouped by category — see the endpoint docs for a full breakdown.

campaignId.description: The ID of the campaign the webhook is associated with (if any)

zapId.description: Zapier integration ID (if the destination is a Zapier webhook)

disabled.description: `true` when the webhook no longer fires. lemlist sets it automatically after a failed delivery, and it can also be toggled from the app. A disabled webhook still occupies one slot of the 200-webhook cap — delete it to free the slot.

disabledReason.description: Why the webhook was disabled. `deliveryError` means lemlist disabled it after a failed delivery. Absent when a user disabled it from the app.

lastErrorStatus.description: What the delivery that caused the deactivation ran into: the HTTP status your endpoint answered (`404`, `410`) or the network error raised while reaching it (`ENOTFOUND`, `ECONNREFUSED`)

Report.description: Aggregated campaign performance statistics (sent, opened, clicked, replied, etc.).

Mailbox.description: An email account connected to a user for sending campaigns.

totalRecords.description: Total number of schedules across all pages

nextPage.description: Next page number (null if on last page)

CrmFilter.description: A filter used in the CRM to segment leads or companies.

InboxConversation.description: A message thread between a user and a contact in the inbox.

InboxConversationPagination.description: Paginated response containing multiple inbox conversations.

InboxMessage.description: A single message within an inbox conversation.

InboxMessagePagination.description: Paginated response containing multiple inbox messages.

Label.description: A label used to categorize and organize inbox conversations.

color.description: Hex color code for the label

createdAt.description: Date and time when the label was created

createdBy.description: Email of the user who created the label

page.description: Value of the `page` query parameter, as sent (a string). The number `0` when the parameter is omitted.

TaskV2.description: A task as returned by `GET /v2/tasks`. Every key is always present — `null` rather than omitted.

objectType.description: Which record the task hangs off, derived from the ids

recordId.description: Id of that record — the company id for a company task, the contact id (or the lead id) otherwise

companyId.description: Company id of the task, or of its contact

assignedTo.description: Id of the user the task is assigned to

message.description: Body of the task

text.description: Body of the reply that opened the task — `opportunityReplied` tasks only

completedAt.description: Date the task was done or ignored

manual.description: True when the task comes from a manual campaign step

ownerName.description: Full name of the assigned user

field.description: Field id, as used in an `advancedFilters` condition

type.description: Data type, which decides the allowed operators

custom.description: True for a custom field of the team

queryParam.description: Flat query parameter addressing this field; `null` means `advancedFilters` only

TaskV2Error.description: Error envelope of the v2 task routes.

message.description: What was wrong, and what is allowed

DatabaseFilter.description: A filter usable in the People and Companies database searches, as listed by Get Database Filters.

filterId.description: Filter identifier, to send as `filterId` in the search filters

description.description: Human-readable filter name, followed by a description of what the filter matches when one exists
description.example: Department: Filter by the lead's department (e.g. 'Sales', 'Marketing', 'Engineering', 'Finance / Legal / Admin', 'Human Resources'). Use to target a functional buyer persona regardless of the exact job title.

mode.description: Search modes the filter can be used in: `leads` for Search People Database, `companies` for Search Companies Database. Omitted when the request is scoped to a single `mode`.

type.description: Kind of input the filter expects. `level` is a two-level dropdown of the People Database UI; it is reported as `select` by default.

values.description: Allowed values, for the filters that have a fixed list

PeopleSchema.description: A person record from lemlist's People database.

lead_id.description: Numeric identifier for the person in the People database

technologies.description: Technologies used by the company, on current experiences only (no `date_to`). Capped at the 100 most recently detected; `technologies_total` gives the full count

first_seen_at.description: When the technology was first detected at the company

technologies_total.description: Number of technologies the company uses, before the cap on `technologies`. Current experiences only

active_job_post.description: Job postings the company currently publishes, on current experiences only. Counts are integers sent as strings

CompaniesSchema.description: A company record from lemlist's Companies database.

company_type.description: Company type (e.g., Privately Held, Public Company)

techno_used_array.description: Array of technologies used by the company

Persona.description: A People Database persona: a named, reusable set of People Database filters saved by your team. A persona id can be referenced elsewhere in the API, for example through the `persona` filter of a Signal Agent.

name.description: Display name. Unique within your team.

filters.description: People Database filters defining the persona

PersonaFilter.description: One People Database filter, as stored in a persona or a saved search. `in` includes matching values, `out` excludes them. There is no `type` property: it is derived from `filterId` server-side.

filterId.description: People Database filter identifier. Use [Get Database Filters](/api-reference/endpoints/people-database/get-database-filters) to discover the valid ids.

exactMatch.description: Exact-match toggle, for the text filters that support it

data.description: The team's personas, most recently created first

deleted.description: Always `true` when the persona was removed

PersonaError.description: Error envelope returned by the persona, saved-search and Get Database Filters endpoints.

code.description: Machine-readable error code, stable across releases

SavedSearch.description: A People Database saved search: a named set of People Database filters saved by your team. It appears in the "Saved searches" menu of the People Database.

name.description: Display name. Unique within your team.

mode.description: Search mode the filters target. Always set: saved searches created before modes existed read as `leads`.

filters.description: People Database filters of the saved search. Same shape as the search endpoints accept, so they can be sent back as is to [Search People Database](/api-reference/endpoints/people-database/search-people-database) or [Search Companies Database](/api-reference/endpoints/people-database/search-companies-database).

createdAt.description: Date the saved search was created

lastResultsCount.description: Number of results the saved search returned the last time it was saved or run

data.description: The team's saved searches, sorted by name

_id.description: Id of the created saved search
Id of the deleted saved search

deleted.description: Always `true` when the saved search was removed

WarmupError.description: A mailbox kept out of warmup, with the cause and the fix.

mailboxId.description: The user mailbox id. Use it as `userMailboxId` to resume warmup with [Start lemwarm](/api-reference/endpoints/lemwarm/start-lemwarm).

email.description: The sending address of the mailbox.

state.description: `paused`: warmup is stopped until the cause is fixed. `warning`: temporary lock, warmup resumes on its own.

since.description: When the cause was recorded. Absent when the state carries no date (DNS lock).

key.description: The catalogued cause. Absent when the stored code is not catalogued yet; `code` then holds the raw value.

code.description: The raw code shown in the lemlist notification, for support.

action.description: The one-click fix in the app: reconnect the mailbox, run the technical setup audit, or resume warmup. Absent when only support can help.

whatToCheck.description: What to verify before resuming warmup.

warmDailyVarianceEnabled.description: Whether a random daily variance is applied to the warmup email target

SignalSchema.description: A signal detected by a Signal Agent representing a tracked event (hiring, LinkedIn activity, website visit, etc.)

teamId.description: Team ID that owns this signal

watchListId.description: ID of the Signal Agent associated with this signal

watchListName.description: Name of the Signal Agent associated with this signal

status.description: Signal status (computed based on user actions)

createdAt.description: When the signal was created in the database

contact.description: Contact associated with this signal (if entity type is 'contact')

signalData.description: Signal-specific data that varies by signal type. Each field is prefixed with the signal type(s) that populate it.

startDate.description: [jobChange/newHire/competitorConnections] Start date at the tracked company

warmIntrosIntroStrength.description: [warmIntros] Intro strength score of the best intro path, from 0 to 100

warmIntrosIntroTier.description: [warmIntros] Intro tier, one of strong, likely or possible

warmIntrosIntroPathsCount.description: [warmIntros] Number of intro paths found for the lead

warmIntrosIntroType.description: [warmIntros] Type of the best intro path

warmIntrosIntroducerName.description: [warmIntros] Name of the introducer of the best path

warmIntrosSharedCompany.description: [warmIntros] Company where the introducer and the lead worked together

warmIntrosSharedCompanyLinkedinUrl.description: [warmIntros] LinkedIn URL of the shared company

warmIntrosSharedCompanyEmployeeCount.description: [warmIntros] Employee count of the shared company

warmIntrosOverlapStart.description: [warmIntros] Start of the overlap period, YYYY-MM

warmIntrosOverlapEnd.description: [warmIntros] End of the overlap period, YYYY-MM

warmIntrosOverlapMonths.description: [warmIntros] Months the introducer and the lead worked together

warmIntrosSameFunction.description: [warmIntros] Whether the introducer and the lead had the same function

WatchListApiFetchSignalsResponse.description: Paginated response containing signals detected by Signal Agents

type.description: Signal type monitored by this Signal Agent

segmentType.description: How the monitored entities are sourced

signalOpportunityTemplate.description: Task/opportunity template applied to each signal when signalProcessingType is create_opportunity.

ownerType.description: Who the created opportunity is assigned to

ownerId.description: Owner user id, when ownerType is specific_owner

message.description: Message body

filters.description: Filters narrowing which entities/events are tracked

emoji.description: Emoji shown next to the agent name

displayInSignalPanel.description: `externalSignalCustomFieldMapping` only: show the custom field in the signal panel.

PageMeta.description: Pagination block of a list response. `totalPages` is at least 1: an empty result is page 1 of 1.

totalPages.description: Total number of pages, at least 1

DeliverabilityAlert.description: A deliverability alert configuration. The alert is evaluated periodically against your warm-up or outreach metrics and triggers notifications through the configured channels (in-app, email, webhook, Slack) when the threshold is breached.

teamId.description: ID of the team that owns the alert.

createdBy.description: ID of the user who created the alert.

widget.description: Data source the alert evaluates. `warmup` checks lemwarm metrics; `outreach` checks campaign-sending metrics.

metric.description: Metric being monitored. Valid combinations depend on `widget`: `warmup` supports `inboxRate`, `spamRate`, `score`; `outreach` supports `deliveryRate`, `bounceRate`.

scope.description: Aggregation level the metric is computed at. `global` covers all of the workspace's mailboxes (warm-up only); `mailbox` evaluates each mailbox individually; `domain` groups mailboxes by their sending domain.

scopeEntities.description: Restricts the alert to a subset of entities matching `scope`. When empty, all entities of that scope are checked. For `scope=mailbox`, each entry is a composite string `userId|email|mailboxId`. For `scope=domain`, each entry is a domain (e.g. `acme.com`). Ignored when `scope=global`.

threshold.description: Threshold value the metric is compared against (0–100, expressed as a percentage for rate metrics).

comparisonOperator.description: How `threshold` is compared to the current value. `below` triggers when the value drops under the threshold; `above` triggers when it exceeds it; `equal` triggers on exact match.

periodDays.description: Length of the evaluation window, in days (1–30).

periodMode.description: How the metric is computed over `periodDays`. `rolling` averages the metric across the window; `consecutive` requires the condition to hold on every one of the most recent `periodDays`.

channelConfig.description: Notification channels triggered when the alert fires. At least one channel must be enabled. If omitted on creation, defaults to `inapp` only.

addresses.description: Required when `email.enabled` is `true`. At least one valid address.

enabled.description: Show the alert in the lemlist app.
Send a webhook callback. Requires a webhook subscribed to the `deliverabilityAlertTriggered` event (see [Add Webhook](/api-reference/endpoints/webhooks/add-webhook)).
Send a Slack message. Requires a Slack integration to be connected on the team.
Whether the alert is currently active. Disabled alerts are not evaluated.

lastCheckedAt.description: Last time the alert was evaluated.

recheckDelayHours.description: Cool-down between re-evaluations after the alert has triggered, in hours. Defaults to 12.

state.description: `active` while the problem lasts, `resolved` once it cleared

code.description: Error code reported by the provider or by lemwarm, when known

resolvedAt.description: When the problem cleared. Absent while `active`

DeliverabilityIncidentError.description: Error envelope returned by the deliverability incidents endpoint.

reasoning.description: The AI's read-out of the account — why it picked these people, or found nobody.

schema.description: Object where each key is a sequence ID and each value is a sequence object

_id.description: The unique identifier of the sequence

steps.description: Array of steps in the sequence

_id.description: The unique identifier of the step

delay.description: The delay in days before executing this step

emailTemplateId.description: The unique identifier of the email template used for this step

type.description: The type of step (e.g., email, linkedinSend, linkedinInMail, linkedinInvite, conditional)

customName.description: The step's own name, shown instead of its type label ("Email", "Call") wherever the app names the step. Absent when the step has none

index.description: The position of the step in the sequence

sequenceId.description: The unique identifier of the parent sequence

sequenceStep.description: The step number in the sequence

message.description: The message content for the step (plain text for LinkedIn, HTML for email)

subject.description: The email subject line (only for email steps)

altMessage.description: The LinkedIn note sent instead of `message` in specific cases. On a `linkedinInvite` step it is the premium invitation note, used when the sending account has LinkedIn Premium. On a `linkedinSend` or `linkedinVoiceNote` step it is the out-of-network note, sent as a connection request when the lead is not a 1st-degree connection. Returned only when the step carries one and it is not empty

altMessagePremium.description: The premium variant of the out-of-network note, sent instead of `altMessage` when the sending LinkedIn account is Premium or Sales Navigator. Only on `linkedinSend` steps, and returned only when it is not empty

abTest.description: A/B test state for this step. `true` while the test runs (leads are split between variant A and B); `"A"` or `"B"` once a winner is selected; absent or `false` when there is no A/B test. `subject` and `message` are always variant A's — read variant B via Get A/B Test Variant

emailTemplateBId.description: Email template ID of variant B (present when an A/B test exists on the step)

conditions.description: The branches of a condition step, in execution order with the Else branch last (only on steps of type `conditional`). Each entry owns the sub-sequence its leads walk; look that `sequenceId` up in this same response to read the branch's own steps. Use `GET /sequences/{sequenceId}/steps/{stepId}/branches` to read the same branches as structured parameters instead of raw selectors.

sequenceId.description: The branch's sub-sequence id - the key to look up in this response, and the branch's address on the branch endpoints

key.description: The condition the step tests. Every branch of a step shares it; absent on the Else branch

label.description: The server-stamped description of what is tested ("If lead variable \"jobTitle\" contains \"CEO\""). On a step with several branches it doubles as the branch's name when `name` is unset

name.description: The branch's display name, present only when someone has set one. The "Branch 1", "Branch 2", … and "Else" defaults lemlist shows are not stored

fallback.description: `true` on the Else branch, which catches every lead no other branch matched and always comes last

delay.description: Length of the time window the condition waits on the lead's action, in days. Only on lead-action conditions

delayType.description: How the condition waits: `within` branches once the window is over, `waitUntil` parks the lead until the action happens

selector.description: The raw stored condition selector, as JSON. Present when the condition carries no time window to hydrate - `customLeadInfo` and `hasEmailAddress` always keep it

level.description: The nesting level of the sequence (0 for main sequence, 1+ for nested conditional sequences)

parentId.description: The unique identifier of the parent sequence (only for conditional sequences)

conditionalStepIndex.description: The index of the conditional step that triggers this sequence (only for conditional sequences)

type.description: The type of step to create

index.description: The position within the sequence to insert the new step (≥ -1). If omitted or greater than the number of steps, the new step is added to the end. On a campaign leads have entered, a step inserted before an existing one moves the leads waiting on that step onto the new one; leads already past that position never receive it.

delay.description: Delay in days before executing this step. Defaults to 0 for the first step and 1 for subsequent steps

subject.description: Email subject line (for email steps). Optional: omit it or send an empty string on a follow-up so the email replies in the thread of the previous one. If no email has been sent to the lead in this campaign yet, it goes out with an empty subject. Required on `linkedinInMail` steps, where it is the InMail subject: a blank one is saved but blocks the campaign launch

message.description: Content of the email or message (used for email, linkedinInvite, linkedinSend, linkedinInMail, manual, phone, whatsappMessage, sms steps, and as the AI script of a linkedinVoiceNote step in `ai` record mode). Required for linkedinSend, linkedinInMail, whatsappMessage, and sms. On a linkedinInMail step it is sent as plain text (LinkedIn does not render HTML), and a blank one is saved but blocks the campaign launch

altMessage.description: The LinkedIn note sent instead of `message` in specific cases, with a meaning that depends on the step type. On `linkedinInvite`: the premium invitation note attached to the connection request, used when the sending account has LinkedIn Premium. On `linkedinSend` and `linkedinVoiceNote`: the out-of-network note, sent as a connection request when the lead is not a 1st-degree connection. Rejected with `400` on any other step type. LinkedIn caps a connection-request note at 200 characters on a free account and 300 on Premium or Sales Navigator. This endpoint does not enforce those caps, but an over-long note is a blocking step error: the campaign refuses to launch until it is shortened

altMessagePremium.description: For `linkedinSend` steps only. The premium variant of the out-of-network note, sent instead of `altMessage` when the sending LinkedIn account is Premium or Sales Navigator (300-character LinkedIn cap). Rejected with `400` on any other step type

customName.description: The step's own name, shown instead of its type label ("Email", "Call") wherever the app names the step. Plain text, up to 70 characters once trimmed and once runs of spaces collapse to one; HTML tags count toward the 70, then are dropped. A longer name is rejected with `400`. Accepted on every step type, ignored on `conditional` steps, which keep their type label

title.description: Title or label for manual steps

url.description: URL of the API endpoint to call (required for api steps). Must start with http:// or https://

customField.description: For conditional steps keyed `customLeadInfo` only. The field to test. A bare name reads as a lead variable (`jobTitle` becomes `variables.jobTitle`); prefix with `fields.` to test a contact field. A company field is written `company.<field>` - `company.name`, or `company.sector` for a company custom field named `Sector` - and `companyName` or `variables.companyName` is stored as `company.name`. `$` and the reserved keys `_id`, `teamId`, `campaignId`, `leadId`, `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype` are refused.

customOperator.description: For conditional steps keyed `customLeadInfo` only. How the field is compared.

customValue.description: For conditional steps keyed `customLeadInfo` only. The value the field is compared to. Required for `equal` and `contains`, and refused for `empty` and `notEmpty`.

campaignId.description: Target campaign ID for sendToAnotherCampaign steps. The campaign must exist and not be archived

leadAction.description: Applies to `sendToAnotherCampaign` steps only. What happens to the lead in the SOURCE campaign once it has been moved to the target one. `continue` keeps it running the remaining steps, `pause` pauses it, `stop` ends the source campaign for it. Omitted leaves the step without a value, which behaves as `continue`; a step added from the lemlist UI defaults to `stop`. A transfer that fails always pauses the lead, whatever this says.

images.description: Public HTTPS URLs of images to attach to a `linkedinInvite` or `linkedinSend` step. lemlist downloads each file and re-hosts it. Allowed MIME types: `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`. Up to 20 MB per file, and up to 6 items total combined with `videos`.

videos.description: Public HTTPS URLs of videos to attach to a `linkedinInvite` or `linkedinSend` step. lemlist downloads each file and re-hosts it. Allowed MIME types: `video/mp4`, `video/quicktime`. Up to 20 MB per file, and up to 6 items total combined with `images`.

skillName.description: Name of the LinkedIn skill to endorse on the lead's profile. Applies to `linkedinEndorse` steps only.

endorseAnyFallback.description: Applies to `linkedinEndorse` steps only. When `true` and the named skill is not on the lead's profile, lemlist falls back to endorsing any available skill.

recordMode.description: Applies to `linkedinVoiceNote` steps only. Determines how the audio is sourced. `manual` (default) means the user records the audio themselves from the lemlist UI after step creation; `ai` means lemlist generates the audio from a text template provided in the lemlist UI.

get.description:
Every branch of a condition step, in execution order, with the Else branch last. A condition step holds an ordered list of branches, each owning the sub-sequence the leads it matches walk into. Array order is execution priority: the first branch whose test matches takes the lead, and the Else branch at the end catches everyone no branch matched. A branch is addressed by its `sequenceId`, never by position - a reorder moves positions, the sub-sequence id is what the runtime routes leads to.

Reading branches is not gated; only the writes are in closed beta.

400.description: `SEQUENCE_BRANCH_STEP_NOT_CONDITIONAL` - the step exists but is not of type `conditional`. `SEQUENCE_BRANCH_INVALID_PARAM` - a path identifier is malformed.

example.error: This step is not a condition step

405.description: Method not allowed - this path accepts GET, POST and PATCH

post.description:
Adds a branch to a condition step, just before the Else branch, and mints the empty sub-sequence it routes to. Add steps to that branch by calling `POST /sequences/{sequenceId}/steps` with the returned `sequenceId`.

A branch carries the value it tests from the moment it is created - there are no blank branches - so the body must say what this one matches. The step's condition is shared by every branch and is never sent here: `conditionKey` in the body is refused.

Only four conditions host several branches: `customLeadInfo`, `hasScore`, `hasEmailAddress` and `aircallDone`. Each needs its own tested value in the body, except `hasScore`, whose new branch inherits a complete `>= 80` band and can be added from an empty body.

name.description: The branch's display name. An empty string clears it, and lemlist falls back to labelling the branch "Branch 1", "Branch 2", … by rank. The Else branch cannot be named.

delayType.description: How a lead-action condition waits: `within` branches once the `delay` window is over, `waitUntil` parks the lead until the action happens, with no time bound. Ignored by the conditions that store no time window (`customLeadInfo`, `hasEmailAddress`).

delay.description: Length of that time window, in days.

scoreComparator.description: `hasScore` only - how the lead's score is compared to `scoreThreshold`.

scoreThreshold.description: `hasScore` only - the score this branch tests against.

emailStatusFilter.description: `hasEmailAddress` only - the email statuses this branch matches. Required to add a branch on that condition.

callStatusFilter.description: `aircallDone` only - the call-status keys this branch matches. The keys are the team's own (defaults plus custom dispositions), so any non-empty string is accepted. Required to add a branch on that condition.

customField.description: `customLeadInfo` only - the field to test. A bare name reads as a lead variable (`jobTitle` becomes `variables.jobTitle`); prefix with `fields.` to test a contact field. A company field is written `company.<field>` - `company.name`, or `company.sector` for a company custom field named `Sector` - and `companyName` or `variables.companyName` is stored as `company.name`. On a step that already tests `variables.companyName`, the new branch keeps that form. Every branch of a step tests the same field, so changing it here changes it on all of them.

customOperator.description: `customLeadInfo` only - how the field is compared. `equal` and `contains` need a `customValue`; `empty` and `notEmpty` refuse one.

customValue.description: `customLeadInfo` only - the value the field is compared to. Required for `equal` and `contains`, and refused for `empty` and `notEmpty`.

400.description: The body or the step cannot host the branch. `SEQUENCE_BRANCH_VALUE_REQUIRED` - the condition needs a tested value the body did not carry. `SEQUENCE_BRANCH_CONDITION_NOT_CONFIGURABLE` - the condition has no branch parameters on the API. `SEQUENCE_BRANCH_CONDITION_KEY_NOT_ALLOWED` - `conditionKey` was sent. `not-multi-capable` - the condition supports a single branch plus Else. `cap-reached` - the step is at its 200-entry ceiling. `SEQUENCE_BRANCH_INVALID_PARAM` - a malformed body or path identifier. A bad `customField`, `customOperator` or `customValue` answers with a plain message and no `code` - for instance `customValue is required for operator "contains"`.

Rewrites the execution priority of a condition step's branches. Order is priority: the first branch whose test matches takes the lead.

`order` must list every non-fallback branch of the step exactly once. The Else branch is not orderable and always stays last, so it is left out of the list. Sending the order the step already has is a no-op that still returns the branches.

patch.description:
Renames a branch and/or changes what it tests. Send only the halves you want to change.

The two halves are gated differently once leads have entered the campaign: a rename still goes through, while re-selecting what the branch tests is refused with `409`. A body that does both on a running campaign is refused whole - the request is atomic, so the rename does not land either. Send the rename on its own if that is what you need.

`conditionKey` is refused: every branch of a step shares the step's condition. The Else branch is neither renamable nor editable.

name.description: The branch's display name. An empty string clears it, and lemlist falls back to labelling the branch "Branch 1", "Branch 2", … by rank. The Else branch cannot be named.

delay.description: Length of that time window, in days.

scoreComparator.description: `hasScore` only - how the lead's score is compared to `scoreThreshold`.

scoreThreshold.description: `hasScore` only - the score this branch tests against.

emailStatusFilter.description: `hasEmailAddress` only - the email statuses this branch matches. Required to add a branch on that condition.

callStatusFilter.description: `aircallDone` only - the call-status keys this branch matches. The keys are the team's own (defaults plus custom dispositions), so any non-empty string is accepted. Required to add a branch on that condition.

customField.description: `customLeadInfo` only - the field to test. A bare name reads as a lead variable (`jobTitle` becomes `variables.jobTitle`); prefix with `fields.` to test a contact field. A company field is written `company.<field>` - `company.name`, or `company.sector` for a company custom field named `Sector` - and `companyName` or `variables.companyName` is stored as `company.name`. Every branch of a step tests the same field, so changing it here changes it on all of them.

customOperator.description: `customLeadInfo` only - how the field is compared. `equal` and `contains` need a `customValue`; `empty` and `notEmpty` refuse one.

customValue.description: `customLeadInfo` only - the value the field is compared to. Required for `equal` and `contains`, and refused for `empty` and `notEmpty`.

A bad `customField`, `customOperator` or `customValue` answers with a plain message and no `code` - for instance `customValue is required for operator "contains"`.

post.description:
Use this endpoint to launch a lead that is waiting for review, without having to enable campaign-wide auto-review.

You're auto launching this specific lead, while still enforcing every other launch guard: the campaign must have no step errors, any AI variables required by the campaign must be valid for the lead, and a sender must be available.

No need to enable autolaunch in the campaign.

This endpoint requires an `emailPro` plan or higher.

Retrying is safe once a call has completed: a lead that is already launched is refused with `CAMPAIGN_LEAD_REVIEW_LEAD_ALREADY_REVIEWED`, so it is never launched twice. Do not send concurrent calls for the same lead.

Possible `error` codes: `CAMPAIGN_LEAD_REVIEW_LEAD_PAUSED` (lead is paused), `CAMPAIGN_LEAD_REVIEW_LEAD_NOT_SCANNED` (lead is still being imported), `CAMPAIGN_LEAD_REVIEW_LEAD_ALREADY_REVIEWED` (lead is not waiting for review, for example already launched), `CAMPAIGN_LEAD_REVIEW_LEAD_AI_VARIABLE_INVALID` (missing or invalid AI variables required by the campaign), `CAMPAIGN_LEAD_REVIEW_LEAD_NO_SENDER_AVAILABLE` (no sender available), `CAMPAIGN_LEAD_REVIEW_CAMPAIGN_NOT_RUNNING` (campaign is archived), `CAMPAIGN_LEAD_REVIEW_CAMPAIGN_STEP_ERRORS` (campaign has step errors).

get.description:
Retrieves CRM sync history: every operation lemlist ran with your CRM (creation, update, activity, association…), newest first, with its outcome and the CRM's error message when it failed. Internal steps of the sync engine are not listed. Available from the Email Pro plan.

**For one record**, pass `contactId` or `companyId`, not both: you get its whole history, with every CRM it was synced with, as the CRM logs filter of its Activities tab shows it. A company's history does not include the operations about its contacts: read them with `contactId`. A record without logs, or an id your team does not have (unknown, deleted or merged into another record), answers `200` with an empty `data`.

**For your whole team**, pass neither: you get the operations with your connected CRM over a period of 31 days at most, the last 31 days by default, as Settings → Integrations → CRM → Logs shows them. A team without a connected CRM answers `200` with an empty `data`. Operations logged at the same instant have no fixed order in this list, so across pages one of them can be repeated or skipped.

parameters.name: contactId
parameters.description: The contact whose history to read (`ctc_xxx`). Pass `contactId` or `companyId`, not both; without either, the team's history is listed. An empty value answers `INVALID_PARAMETER`.

parameters.name: companyId
parameters.description: The company whose history to read (`cpn_xxx`). Pass `contactId` or `companyId`, not both; without either, the team's history is listed. An empty value answers `INVALID_PARAMETER`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, starting at 1. Default: 1. `page × limit` must not exceed 5,000 (`PAGE_OUT_OF_RANGE`): beyond the 5,000 most recent rows, call again with `to` set to the `createdAt` of the last log you received. `to` is inclusive, so the logs of that instant come back: skip the `_id`s you already have.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of logs per page, from 1 to 100. Default: 100.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only the logs in these states, comma-separated: `pending`, `done`, `error`, `aborted`. When the parameter is repeated, the last value is used.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Only the logs of these categories, comma-separated: `contact`, `company`, `association`, `activity`, `email`, `linkedin`, `sms`, `whatsapp`, `call`, `note`, `task`, `deal`, `event`.

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: Only the logs of these operations, comma-separated, by their `method` name (see `CrmLog.method`). A name covers both directions: `contact_update` is a lemlist write and a change received from the CRM. With `category`, both filters apply. When the parameter is repeated, the last value is used.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Only the logs created at or after this date (ISO 8601, read in UTC: a time without offset is UTC, a date without time starts at 00:00). For a record, no default: its whole history. For the team, 31 days before `to` by default, and `from` and `to` may span 31 days at most (`INVALID_DATE_RANGE`): with dates without time, `from=2026-08-01&to=2026-08-31` is the widest window.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Only the logs created at or before this date (ISO 8601, read in UTC: a time without offset is UTC, a date without time covers that whole day, up to 23:59:59.999). Default: now.

hasMore.description: Whether older logs exist past this page. For a contact or a company, it stays `false` on the page ending at row 5,000, even when older logs exist. For the team, it says whether they exist, and the next page answers `PAGE_OUT_OF_RANGE`. Past row 5,000, call again with `to`.
