post.description:
Links a campaign to a filter of your connected CRM and imports its records as leads.

**Recurring:** the campaign stays linked to the filter, and the records the filter picks up later are imported automatically.

**New link only:** the campaign must not be linked to a CRM filter yet. Changing or unlinking a campaign's CRM filter is done in the lemlist app.

The filter is checked in your CRM before anything is saved. The import runs in the background: leads appear over the next minutes, not in the response.

**Credits:** the enrichments requested in `enrichFeature` run on every imported lead, now and later, and are charged to the user of the API key.

filterType.description: Salesforce only: `lead` or `contact` list views, or `report`. Ignored by HubSpot and Pipedrive. Defaults to `lead` when your Salesforce connection allows Leads, `contact` otherwise.

userId.description: Salesforce only, for a list view scoped to its owner ("My leads", "My contacts"…): the team member the view is read as. They must have their own Salesforce account connected in lemlist. Leave it out in every other case (reports, views not scoped to an owner); it is ignored for HubSpot and Pipedrive, where your team's CRM connection is used.

deduplicate.description: `all` (or `true`) skips contacts already in another campaign, `activeOnly` skips only contacts still active in another campaign, `off` (or `false`, the default) imports everyone.

enrichFeature.description: Enrichments to run on every imported lead, as an array or a `|`-separated string (e.g. `find_email|verify`). Consumes credits for each lead.

200.description: The campaign is linked to the filter; the import runs in the background.

400.description: The request was refused; `error` explains why (e.g. `This campaign already imports from a CRM filter: ...`, `CRM filter not found: ...`, `CRM not connected: ...`, `User not in team`, `Bad params`, `Unsupported enrichment features`, `Upgrade your plan to use this feature`, or a credit refusal for the requested enrichments).

post.description:
This endpoint allows you to query our People database. To do so, you may use the following parameters: filters (required, unless `fromSearchId` is provided), fromSearchId (optional), page (optional), size (optional), and excludes (optional). Each filter should have the following properties: filterId (filter identifier), in (list of the values you want to include), and out (list of the values you want to exclude). To know which filters you are able to use, refer to the GET Filters section. To run a previous search again, pass the `search` id it returned as `fromSearchId`.

The `department` filter accepts the following values: `Sales`, `Customer service`, `Engineering`, `Marketing`, `Operations`, `Human Resources`, `Finance / Legal / Admin`, `Other`.

requestBody.description: Search criteria. Provide one or more filters and optionally control pagination with page/size

filters.description: Array of filters (required, unless `fromSearchId` is provided). With `fromSearchId`, each filter replaces the saved filter with the same `filterId` and the other saved filters are kept; an empty or absent `filters` replays the search as is.

in.description: List of the values you want to include

out.description: List of the values you want to exclude

fromSearchId.description:
Id of a previous People search of your team (not a Companies search): the `search` value returned by `POST /database/people` (optional). The search is replayed with its saved filters. Each filter you pass in `filters` replaces the saved filter with the same `filterId`, the other saved filters are kept, and the merged filters are validated again as for a new search. With `fromSearchId`, `filters` is optional: an empty or absent `filters` replays the search as is.

A `search` id can be replayed for 6 months. A replay counts as one search in the daily search quota (see `limitation` in the response); only a paid part triggered elsewhere, such as LinkedIn post engagement, is not billed again.

If no search matches this id for your team and this mode, or the search is older than 6 months, the request is rejected with 404.

excludes.description: Array of properties to exclude from the results (optional)

post.description:
Finds the people who commented on or reacted to a LinkedIn post and returns them as People Database rows, in a single call.

The post is read first, then the engagers are searched in the People Database. Comments are collected before reactions, the post author is excluded and the slugs are deduplicated, for at most 1000 people. `filters` are applied to the engagers in the same search, for example to keep one country.

This endpoint is paid: each call debits 50 credits once the post has been read, even when the search finds nobody. A `200` always means credits were debited, and no error code debits credits.

The response carries a `search` id. To get the next pages or to refine the filters, send it as `fromSearchId` to `POST /database/people`. This debits no credits, but it counts in the 24-hour People Database search quota, like any search. Do not call this endpoint again on the same post for that, it would be billed again.

requestBody.description: The LinkedIn post to read, and optionally the filters to apply to its engagers. Unknown keys are rejected with 400.

url.description: Link of the LinkedIn post. Prefer the post page (`linkedin.com/posts/...`). A short `lnkd.in` link or a `linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:...` link also works, but a feed/update link can fail on a post published in the last few hours.

type.description: Which engagers to collect. `all` collects the comments first, then the reactions.

filters.description: People Database leads filters (optional), applied to the engagers in the same search, for example a country. They are validated before any credit is debited. `linkedinPostEngagement` and `leadLinkedInSlug` are rejected with 400, the search sets them itself.

size.description: Number of People Database rows returned in `data.people`, between 1 and 100 (optional).

200.description: The post was read and 50 credits were debited

slugs.description: LinkedIn slugs of the engagers, post author excluded and deduplicated

totals.description: Totals announced by LinkedIn for the requested `type`

comments.description: Number of comments on the post

reactions.description: Number of reactions on the post

isCapped.description: `true` when the post had more than 1000 engagers

filters.description: Exact filters of the People Database search: `leadLinkedInSlug` plus the filters you passed. Empty when nobody engaged with the post.

search.description: Id of the People Database search. Send it as `fromSearchId` to `POST /database/people` to get the next pages or refine the filters. This debits no credits, but it counts in the 24-hour People Database search quota, like any search. Absent when nobody engaged with the post.

people.description: First page of the People Database search, in the format of `POST /database/people`. Absent when nobody engaged with the post or when the People Database search failed.

peopleSearchFailed.description: Present and `true` when the credits were debited and `slugs` exist, but the People Database search failed. Run `POST /database/people` yourself with `filters`.

Each filter you pass in `filters` replaces the saved filter with the same `filterId`, the other saved filters are kept, and the merged filters are validated again as for a new search. With `fromSearchId`, `filters` is optional: an empty or absent `filters` replays the search as is.

A `search` id can be replayed for 6 months. A replay counts as one search in the daily search quota (see `limitation` in the response); only a paid part triggered elsewhere, such as LinkedIn post engagement, is not billed again.

If no search matches this id for your team and this mode, or the search is older than 6 months, the request is rejected with 404.

get.description:
Exports the People Database leads matching a search as a CSV file. The response is streamed as `text/csv` with a `Content-Disposition: attachment` header.

The export is defined by the search itself — there is no hand-picked selection: rows come back in the team's stable search order, capped by `limit`.

**Billing** — charged on the team's existing 24h search quota, one unit per 100 exported rows (an export of 1000 rows costs 10). Nothing is charged if the export fails.

**Caps** — 1000 rows maximum; a higher `limit` is rejected with a 400. Free-trial and freemium teams are capped lower, at one page (100 rows), matching the search window their plan allows.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description:
The search to export, URL-encoded JSON array — the same `filters` array `POST /database/people` takes. Each entry needs a `filterId` and at least one `in`/`out` value.

Filter ids and their allowed values come from `GET /database/filters`. That endpoint returns `values` only for filters with a closed list; filters of type `autocomplete` (job titles, companies, countries, skills, technologies…) have no enumerable list, so their values are discovered by running a search rather than read upfront.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many rows to export. Defaults to 1000, which is also the maximum.

Renames a saved search and/or replaces its filters. At least one of `name` and `filters` is required.

`filters` replace the saved filters entirely: they are not merged. `mode` is only read together with `filters` and defaults to the current mode of the saved search. Filters incompatible with the `mode` or with your team's plan are dropped silently; if none remain, the request answers `400`.

get.description: Retrieve tasks with optional filtering and pagination. Tasks marked as `done` are excluded from results.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number for paginated results (0-indexed).

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description:
JSON array of filter objects. Each filter has a `filterId` and specific parameters.

**Available Filters:**

- `fullName`: Filter by contact's full name.
  - Parameters: `value` (string) or `regex` (string)
  - Example: `{"filterId":"fullName","value":"John Doe"}`

- `email`: Filter by contact's email address.
  - Parameters: `value` (string) or `regex` (string)
  - Example: `{"filterId":"email","value":"john@example.com"}`

- `phone`: Filter by contact's phone number.
  - Parameters: `value` (string) or `regex` (string)
  - Example: `{"filterId":"phone","value":"+1234567890"}`

- `linkedin`: Filter by LinkedIn profile URL.
  - Parameters: `value` (string) or `regex` (string)
  - Example: `{"filterId":"linkedin","value":"linkedin.com/in/johndoe"}`

- `campaignId`: Filter by campaign IDs (inclusion/exclusion).
  - Parameters: `in` (array of strings) and/or `out` (array of strings)
  - Example: `{"filterId":"campaignId","in":["cam_123"],"out":["cam_456"]}`

- `campaignState`: Filter by campaign states.
  - Parameters: `in` (array of strings) and/or `out` (array of strings)
  - Allowed values: `draft`, `running`, `ended`, `paused`, `errors`, `archived`
  - Example: `{"filterId":"campaignState","in":["running","paused"]}`

- `type`: Filter by task type.
  - Parameters: `in` (array of strings) and/or `out` (array of strings)
  - Allowed values: `manual`, `phone`, `linkedinInvite`, `linkedinSend`, `linkedinVoiceNote`, `emailsReplied`, `opportunityReplied`, `linkedinReplied`, `opportunityClicked`, `email`, `whatsappMessage`
  - Example: `{"filterId":"type","in":["phone","email"]}`

- `assignedTo`: Filter by assigned user IDs.
  - Parameters: `in` (array of strings) and/or `out` (array of strings)
  - Example: `{"filterId":"assignedTo","in":["usr_123","usr_456"]}`

- `dueDate`: Filter by due date range.
  - Parameters: `from` (string, YYYY-MM-DD) and/or `to` (string, YYYY-MM-DD)
  - Example: `{"filterId":"dueDate","from":"2025-01-01","to":"2025-12-31"}`

Multiple filters can be combined in an array.

post.description: Create a manual task (opportunity) associated with a contact/company or lead.

recordId.description: ID of the record the task is about: a contact (`ctc_`), a company (`cpn_`) or a lead (`lea_`). Required unless the legacy `leadId` is sent. A company task can only be of type `manual`.

leadId.description: Legacy name of `recordId`, still accepted for backward compatibility. Use `recordId` instead. When both are sent, `leadId` is used.

assignedTo.description: The ID of the team member assigned to the task (userId).

dueDate.description: The due date in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2025-02-12T00:00:00.000Z). A date in the past is accepted: the task is created already due.

title.description: Optional title of the task. Defaults to an empty string if omitted.

message.description: Optional instruction of the task, returned as `content` in the response. Defaults to an empty string if omitted. On a `linkedin` task for a lead (`lea_` ID), it also pre-fills the draft when `taskData.content` is omitted.

taskData.description: Draft of the message to send on `email`, `linkedin` and `whatsapp` tasks, and fallback number on `phone` tasks.

subject.description: Subject of the email. Only used on `email` tasks, ignored on other types.

content.description: Draft of the message to send. Only used on `email`, `linkedin` and `whatsapp` tasks, ignored on other types. Must stay under 1 MB, measured in bytes once UTF-8 encoded (1,000,000 bytes).

phone.description: On a `phone` task, number the lemlist dialer offers when neither the contact nor the lead has one. Ignored on other types.

images.description: Public HTTPS URLs of images to attach to a `linkedin` task. lemlist downloads each file and re-hosts it. On other types they are not downloaded, but still count toward the limit of 6. Allowed MIME types: `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`. Up to 20 MB per file, and up to 6 items total combined with `videos`.

videos.description: Public HTTPS URLs of videos to attach to a `linkedin` task. lemlist downloads each file and re-hosts it. On other types they are not downloaded, but still count toward the limit of 6. Allowed MIME types: `video/mp4`, `video/quicktime`. Up to 20 MB per file, and up to 6 items total combined with `images`.

200.description: The created task. The `message` you sent is returned as `content` and `assignedTo` as `userId`. A `linkedin` or `whatsapp` task comes back with its internal type, `linkedinSend` or `whatsappMessage`. `priority` comes back as a number (`0`, `1` or `2`) and is omitted when empty.

400.description:
The body is `{ "error": "<message>" }`, where the message is one of:

- `One of your fields is invalid or missing` - `type`, `dueDate` or `assignedTo` is missing or invalid (`assignedTo` must be a user ID), `priority` is not one of the accepted values, `title` or `message` is not a string, `images` / `videos` is not an array of strings, `taskData` is not an object, or `recordId` / `leadId` is not a well-formed ID.
- `recordId is required` - neither `recordId` nor `leadId` was sent.
- `recordId is invalid` - the ID does not start with `ctc_`, `cpn_` or `lea_`.
- A message starting with `Match error:` - `title` is longer than 400 characters, `message` is longer than 32,000 characters, `taskData.subject` is not a string or is longer than 400 characters on an `email` task, `taskData.content` is not a string on an `email`, `linkedin` or `whatsapp` task, `taskData.phone` is not a string, or a company task is not of type `manual`.
- `No contact, company or lead found for this id in the team` - the record does not exist in your team.
- `The assignee is not a member of the team` - `assignedTo` is not a member of your team.
- `The message content is too big (max 1 MB)` - `taskData.content` reaches 1,000,000 bytes once UTF-8 encoded, on an `email`, `linkedin` or `whatsapp` task.
- `dueDate must be a valid future ISO 8601 date` - `dueDate` is exactly the Unix epoch (`1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`). Other past dates are accepted.
- `LINKEDIN_MEDIA_TOO_MANY` - more than 6 `images` and `videos` combined, whatever the task `type`.
- On a `linkedin` task, a media URL that fails ingestion sets `error` to a JSON-encoded array of items, each with a `url`, `index`, `code` and `message`. The status follows the first item's code: 400 for `LINKEDIN_MEDIA_UNSAFE_URL`, the other codes answer with the statuses listed on [Add Step to Sequence](/api-reference/endpoints/sequences/add-step-to-sequence#linkedin-media-constraints).

When no API key is supplied, the answer is the plain text `no api key provided`.

get.description:
Retrieves contacts by IDs/emails or by CRM record ids, or searches/lists contacts by name, email, contact list, campaign membership, or company link.

When using `idsOrEmails`, returns an array of matching contacts directly.

When using `crmIds`, looks the contacts up by their record id in the connected CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive) and returns an array of the contacts found, each with the matched id under `crmSync.crmRecordId`. `idsOrEmails` takes precedence over `crmIds`; a lookup ignores the search filters and the pagination.

When using `search`, `email`, `listId`, `notInAnyCampaign`, any of the `company*` filters, or no filter at all, returns a paginated response with `data`, `total`, `limit`, and `offset` fields. You can combine filters together to narrow results (e.g. `listId` with `search`, or `notInAnyCampaign` with `companyId`). Calling the endpoint without any filter returns all contacts of the team, paginated.

A lookup returns full contacts (`Contact`); the list returns `ContactListItem` objects.

The `company*` filters (`companyId`, `companyDomain`, `companyLinkedinUrl`, `companySalesnavUrl`) are mutually exclusive: use only one at a time. `companyDomain` / `companyLinkedinUrl` / `companySalesnavUrl` are resolved to a `companyId` through the Companies collection; if no matching company exists, the endpoint returns an empty list with `total: 0` (not an error), which keeps automation flows simple.

parameters.name: idsOrEmails
parameters.description: A comma separated string of either valid contact IDs (MongoDB ObjectId) or valid email addresses. Optional — when omitted, returns the paginated list of all contacts of the team. Maximum 100 values.

parameters.name: crmIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated record ids of contacts in the CRM connected to the team (HubSpot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive); for Salesforce, the 18-character Contact or Lead id. Returns an array of the contacts found, each with the matched id under `crmSync.crmRecordId`; ids that match nothing are skipped, and the array is empty when no CRM is connected. Duplicates are removed; an empty value is ignored. Maximum 100 values (`TOO_MANY_CRM_IDS`); a value over 25 characters answers `INVALID_CRM_ID`. Ignored when `idsOrEmails` is provided.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Search contacts by name or other text fields. Must be at least 2 characters.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Search contacts by exact email address.

parameters.name: listId
parameters.description: Filter contacts by contact list ID (`clt_xxx` format). Can be combined with `search` or `email`, or used alone to list all contacts in a list. Get valid IDs from `GET /contacts/lists`.

parameters.name: notInAnyCampaign
parameters.description: When set to `true`, only returns contacts that are not part of any campaign (orphan contacts). Can be used alone or combined with other filters such as `search`, `email`, or `listId`.

parameters.name: companyId
parameters.description: Filter contacts by attached company ID (`cpn_xxx` format). Use this when you already know the lemlist company id (for example after fetching `GET /companies?crmSyncStatus=unique_index_error_company`). Mutually exclusive with `companyDomain`, `companyLinkedinUrl`, and `companySalesnavUrl`.

parameters.name: companyDomain
parameters.description: Filter contacts by their company's website domain. Resolved to a `companyId` against the Companies collection. If no company matches, the endpoint returns an empty list (`total: 0`). Mutually exclusive with the other `company*` filters.

parameters.name: companyLinkedinUrl
parameters.description: Filter contacts by their company's LinkedIn URL. Resolved to a `companyId` against the Companies collection. If no company matches, the endpoint returns an empty list (`total: 0`). Mutually exclusive with the other `company*` filters.

parameters.name: companySalesnavUrl
parameters.description: Filter contacts by their company's LinkedIn Sales Navigator URL. Resolved to a `companyId` against the Companies collection. If no company matches, the endpoint returns an empty list (`total: 0`). Mutually exclusive with the other `company*` filters.

parameters.name: withPrimaryCompany
parameters.description: When set to `true`, only returns contacts linked to a company; when set to `false`, only returns contacts without a company. Omit for no filter. Mutually exclusive with the `company*` filters (`companyId`, `companyDomain`, `companyLinkedinUrl`, `companySalesnavUrl`).

parameters.name: fieldRejectionReason
parameters.description: Filter contacts to those carrying a field rejection with this reason — a value lemlist refused to write, prefixed by its origin (`enrichment_*` while enriching, `crm_sync_*` during CRM sync). Returns an empty list (`total: 0`) when no contact matches. Each returned contact exposes the full detail under `fieldRejections[]` (which field, why, and `conflictingRecordId` for duplicates). Only applies to the paginated list — ignored when `idsOrEmails` is provided (that path returns the exact contacts requested, unfiltered).

parameters.name: crmSyncStatus
parameters.description:
Filter contacts by their CRM sync state against the team's active CRM provider. Requires a CRM (Hubspot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive) to be connected — otherwise the request returns `400 NO_CRM_CONNECTED`. Values:
- `synced` — the contact has a CRM record and no sync errors.
- `not_synced` — the contact has no CRM record yet.
- `searching` — a CRM search (Search & connect, Create in CRM) is queued or running for the contact.
- `not_found` — the last CRM search found no record for the contact.
- `error` — at least one sync error is currently raised, whatever its reason.
- A specific error reason (lowercase form), to filter by root cause:
  - `invalid_email` — the CRM refused the contact's email.
  - `property_doesnt_exist` — a mapped property does not exist in the CRM.
  - `required_field_missing` — a field the CRM requires is missing.
  - `unique_index_error_contact` — the CRM record is already synced with another lemlist contact.
  - `contact_already_exists_with_name`, `contact_already_exists_with_linkedin_url`, `contact_already_exists_with_email` — a CRM contact already exists with the same first and last name, LinkedIn URL or email.
  - `contact_blocked_by_company` — contact not created: its company already exists in the CRM.
  - `contact_blocked_by_company_search` — contact not created: the company search is incomplete, retried later.
  - `contact_blocked_by_company_without_name` — contact not created: its company needs a name to be found in the CRM.
  - `contact_blocked_by_company_without_key` — contact not created: its company needs a domain or LinkedIn URL to be found in the CRM.
  - `contact_blocked_by_company_already_synced` — contact not created: its company is already synced with another lemlist company.

Only applies to the paginated list — ignored when `idsOrEmails` or `crmIds` is provided.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of contacts to return (1–500). Defaults to 100.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of contacts to skip for pagination. Defaults to 0.

200.description: Success. When using `idsOrEmails` or `crmIds`, returns an array of contacts (empty when no `crmIds` value matches). Otherwise, returns a paginated object with `data` (`ContactListItem` items), `total`, `limit`, and `offset`.

fields.leadStatus: Marked as not Interested by api

400.description: Either a plain `{ "error": "..." }` (`Bad team`, search query too short, invalid `listId` format, invalid `withPrimaryCompany`, `limit` below 1, more than 100 `idsOrEmails` values), or a validation envelope. Possible error codes: `INVALID_CRM_ID` (a `crmIds` list with no usable value, or a value longer than 25 characters), `TOO_MANY_CRM_IDS` (more than 100 `crmIds` values), `MULTIPLE_COMPANY_FILTERS`, `INVALID_COMPANY_ID`, `INVALID_FIELD_REJECTION_REASON`, `INVALID_CRM_SYNC_STATUS`, `NO_CRM_CONNECTED` (`crmSyncStatus` without a connected CRM).

value.error: Search query must be at least 2 characters

error.message: Invalid crmId value
crmIds exceeds the maximum of 100 values

text/plain.example: The authentication you supplied is incorrect

404.description: No contact matches the `idsOrEmails` values.

504.description: `READ_TOO_SLOW`: a `crmSyncStatus` read took more than 10 seconds. Without a `listId`, that filter reads every contact of the team: pass a `listId` to narrow it; the same request will time out again.

post.description:
Creates a new contact or updates an existing one (upsert). If a contact with the same email, LinkedIn URL, or Sales Navigator URL already exists, it is updated as the `updateStrategy` query parameter says (by default, sent values replace stored ones and empty values are ignored). You can target an existing contact directly by providing `contactId`, bypassing email/LinkedIn matching. You can optionally link the contact to a company by providing `companyId`, `companyDomain`, or `companyLinkedinUrl`.

**Permission:** creating a contact requires the "Create contacts" permission on the API key's user, otherwise the request fails with `403 CONTACT_CREATE_NOT_ALLOWED`. Updating an existing contact does not.

contactId.description: Existing contact ID. Updates a specific contact by ID, bypassing email/LinkedIn matching. Can only be used to update an existing contact, not to create a new one. When provided, `email` and `linkedinUrl` are not required. At least one of `contactId`, `email`, `linkedinUrl`, or `linkedinUrlSalesNav` is required.

email.description: Contact email address. Used as a unique key for upsert matching. At least one of `contactId`, `email`, `linkedinUrl`, or `linkedinUrlSalesNav` is required.

linkedinUrl.description: LinkedIn profile URL. Used as an alternative unique key for upsert matching. At least one of `contactId`, `email`, `linkedinUrl`, or `linkedinUrlSalesNav` is required.

linkedinUrlSalesNav.description: LinkedIn Sales Navigator profile URL. Used as an alternative unique key for upsert matching.

additionalEmails.description: Additional email addresses for the contact. Each must be a valid email address.

jobTitle.description: Contact job title. If a company is linked, this is saved as part of the job data.

jobDescription.description: Contact job description. If a company is linked, this is saved as part of the job data.

picture.description: URL of the contact's profile picture.

peopleDbSeniority.description: Seniority of the person, from the People Database.

peopleDbDepartment.description: Department of the person, from the People Database.

peopleDbConnectionCount.description: LinkedIn connections count of the person, from the People Database. 500 usually means 500 or more.

contactOwner.description: Owner of the contact. Can be a user ID (e.g. `usr_...`) or a team member's email address. If the provided value does not match a team member, the contact is still written with an `OWNER_NOT_FOUND` or `INVALID_OWNER_FORMAT` entry in `warnings`: the owner defaults to the API key owner on creation and is unchanged on update. On update it replaces the current owner, except under `fillEmptyOnly` where it is only set when the contact has none.

source.description: Origin of the contact record. Set on creation only and cannot be updated afterwards. Defaults to `api`.

companyId.description: ID of a company already existing in lemlist to link to this contact. Takes priority over `companyDomain` and `companyLinkedinUrl`.

companyDomain.description: Domain of a company already existing in lemlist to link to this contact (e.g. `lemlist.com`). Used if `companyId` is not provided.

companyLinkedinUrl.description: LinkedIn URL of a company already existing in lemlist to link to this contact. Used if `companyId` and `companyDomain` are not provided.

crmId.description: Closed beta: refused as an unknown field (`400 INVALID_FIELD`) unless the CRM ID remap beta is enabled for your team. Id of the record of the connected CRM to link the contact to: a HubSpot, Pipedrive or Zoho numeric id (send a Zoho id as a string: its 19 digits are too long for a JSON number), an Attio record id, or a Salesforce Contact (`003…`) or Lead (`00Q…`) id of 15 or 18 characters. Requires an admin API key. A new contact is created already linked; an existing one has its link moved to this record. An id another contact holds updates that contact when the body carries its email or LinkedIn URL, and is refused otherwise. See the endpoint page for the refusals.

additionalProperties.description: Any additional key is treated as a custom field. Custom fields must be registered in the team's CRM field registry beforehand.

200.description: Existing contact updated (upsert matched by email or LinkedIn URL)

data.description: Same shape as the 201 response, with `created: false` and `updated: true`.

warnings.description: Non-blocking notices: owner or company not resolved, or `FIELDS_KEPT` when the update strategy kept values you sent (`params.fields` names them).

code.description: `OWNER_NOT_FOUND` or `INVALID_OWNER_FORMAT` (`contactOwner` matches no team member); `COMPANY_NOT_FOUND_BY_ID`, `COMPANY_NOT_FOUND_BY_DOMAIN` or `COMPANY_NOT_FOUND_BY_LINKEDIN_URL` (company not linked); `FIELDS_KEPT` (values the update strategy kept); `CRM_ID_NOT_APPLIED` (`crmId` not applied: the contact stays linked to another CRM record of the same person, typically a Salesforce Contact facing a Lead id; send its `contactId` to move the link).

params.description: Details: the input echoed back, or `fields` for `FIELDS_KEPT`.

fields.description: Key/value fields (firstName, lastName, phone, jobTitle, custom fields, etc.)

companyId.description: Linked company ID (present only when a company was linked)

createdBy.description: User ID who created the record

created.description: `true` when a new contact was created, `false` when an existing contact was updated.

updated.description: Present and set to `true` only when an existing contact was updated (i.e. `created` is `false`).

companyLinked.description: Whether a company was successfully linked to the contact.

warnings.description: Non-blocking notices: owner or company not resolved, or `FIELDS_KEPT` when the update strategy kept values you sent (`params.fields` names them).

code.description: `OWNER_NOT_FOUND` or `INVALID_OWNER_FORMAT` (`contactOwner` matches no team member); `COMPANY_NOT_FOUND_BY_ID`, `COMPANY_NOT_FOUND_BY_DOMAIN` or `COMPANY_NOT_FOUND_BY_LINKEDIN_URL` (company not linked); `FIELDS_KEPT` (values the update strategy kept); `CRM_ID_NOT_APPLIED` (`crmId` not applied: the contact stays linked to another CRM record of the same person, typically a Salesforce Contact facing a Lead id; send its `contactId` to move the link).

params.description: Details: the input echoed back, or `fields` for `FIELDS_KEPT`.

400.description: Validation error

code.description: Error code: `MISSING_IDENTIFIER`, `INVALID_CONTACT_ID`, `INVALID_EMAIL`, `INVALID_ADDITIONAL_EMAILS`, `INVALID_LINKEDIN_URL`, `INVALID_FIELD`, `INVALID_USER_FIELD_FORMAT`, `USER_FIELD_NOT_FOUND`, `CONTACT_VALIDATION_FAILED`, `INVALID_UPDATE_STRATEGY`, `INVALID_CRM_ID` (`crmId` does not have the format of the connected CRM, or points to another kind of record), or `NO_CRM_CONNECTED` (`crmId` sent while no CRM is connected).

error.message: At least one identifier is required: email, linkedinUrl or contactId

401.description: The authentication you supplied is incorrect

post.description:
Merges up to 10 lemlist contacts into one. The survivor (`primaryId`) keeps its id and every value it holds; its empty fields are filled from the other contacts, which are then deleted. Everything attached to a deleted contact (leads in campaigns, activities, tasks, list memberships, inbox conversations) is moved to the survivor. When a CRM is connected, the survivor keeps its CRM link (or adopts the first linked record's when it has none) and receives the merged values there; lemlist never merges or deletes anything in the CRM itself, so the other records' CRM entries stay in the CRM, unlinked from lemlist — merge them CRM-side too, or a CRM import may recreate the duplicate.

The contacts are folded into the survivor one at a time and the run **stops at the first failure**: `mergedIds` lists what went through, `remainingIds` what still exists. A first-fold failure returns an error instead — nothing was written.

**Email addresses:** the survivor keeps its own; a loser's addresses are dropped, unless the survivor has none (then it takes the first loser's).

**No undo:** deleted contacts are gone.

primaryId.description: The surviving contact. A lemlist contact id (`ctc_xxx`) or one of the contact's email addresses.

secondaryIds.description: The contacts folded into the survivor then deleted, 9 at most. A lemlist contact id (`ctc_xxx`) or one of the contact's email addresses. Must not contain `primaryId`, and each contact is listed once.

200.description: Merge run — **`success: true` does not mean complete.** The contacts fold one at a time and the run stops at the first failure, so ALWAYS check `remainingIds`: the contacts listed there were NOT merged and still exist. Fix the cause (typically an enrichment in progress) and call again with the survivor and the remaining ids.

primaryId.description: ID of the surviving lemlist contact — resolved from the email when one was given.

merged.description: `true` once at least one contact was folded into the survivor.

mergedIds.description: IDs of the contacts folded into the survivor and deleted, in fold order.

remainingIds.description: IDs of the contacts NOT merged because an earlier fold failed. Empty when everything went through.

rejectedFields.description: Fields whose adopted value was refused by a uniqueness rule (kept survivor-side). Only present when it happened.

400.description: Invalid request. Possible error codes: `ENTITY_MERGE_INVALID_PAYLOAD` (missing `primaryId` or empty `secondaryIds`), `ENTITY_MERGE_SAME_ENTITY` (`primaryId` among `secondaryIds`, or a contact listed twice), `ENTITY_MERGE_TOO_MANY_ENTITIES` (more than 9 `secondaryIds`).

error.message: A record cannot be merged with itself, and each record is listed once

post.summary: Search & Connect Contacts in the CRM
post.description:
Searches your connected CRM for each contact and links it to the CRM record found — the **Search & connect** action of the Contacts page. No CRM record is ever created: use `POST /contacts/crm/create` for that. Each contact it links then syncs its mapped fields with that CRM record, which can update it.

Target the contacts with `idsOrEmails` (lemlist ids or email addresses) **or** with `listId` for a whole contact list: 10,000 contacts at most either way.

**Asynchronous:** the call queues the work and answers at once with what was queued, not with what the CRM returned. Each contact's outcome lands on its `crmSync` block shortly after: read it with `GET /contacts?idsOrEmails=...` (100 per call), or, after a list, list its contacts by state with `listId` and `crmSyncStatus`: `searching` while the search runs, then `synced` once linked, or `not_found` when no CRM record matched. Without `listId`, `crmSyncStatus` reads every contact of the team: do not poll it.

- A contact already linked to a CRM record is synced with it again (`alreadyLinked`).
- A contact with nothing to search the CRM with is left untouched (`notSearchable`).
- A contact whose CRM search is already queued is not queued twice (`alreadyInProgress`).

Requires a connected CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive, Attio or Zoho).

listId.description: A contact list id (`clt_xxx`): acts on every contact of the list, static or dynamic, 10,000 at most. Use it instead of `idsOrEmails`.

post.summary: Add or Remove Contacts in a List
post.description:
Adds existing CRM contacts to a static contact list, or removes them when `?action=remove` is set.

- **Add** (default): send a `POST` with a `contactIds` body. Contacts already in the list are silently skipped (no duplicates) and reported in `alreadyInList`.
- **Remove**: send a `POST` with `?action=remove` and a `contactIds` body. Contacts that are not in the list are silently skipped; `removedCount` reflects the associations actually removed. This only affects list membership, the contacts are not deleted from your CRM.

The list must be a **static** contact list (`clt_xxx`). Dynamic lists (auto-populated by filter rules) and company lists are rejected.

**Removal uses `POST ?action=remove` on purpose:** a `DELETE` request body is dropped by our stack, so `DELETE` on this path is **not supported** and returns `405 Method Not Allowed`.

alreadyInList.description: Number of contacts that were already in the list and therefore skipped (add only).

removedCount.description: Number of list associations actually removed (remove only). Contacts that were not in the list are not counted.

get.description:
Retrieves companies by IDs/domains or by CRM record ids, or lists them with filters.

When using `idsOrDomains`, returns the matching companies in `data`, with `total` and no pagination.

When using `crmIds`, looks the companies up by their record id in the connected CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive) and returns them like `idsOrDomains` does, each with the matched id under `crmSync.crmRecordId`.

Otherwise, returns a paginated response with `data`, `total`, `limit`, and `offset`.

`idsOrDomains` takes precedence over `crmIds`; a lookup ignores the list filters and the pagination.

parameters.name: idsOrDomains
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of company IDs or domains to fetch. When provided, returns only matching companies (no pagination). Each value is classified as a company ID (e.g. `cpn_xxx`) or a domain (e.g. `example.com`). URLs are normalized automatically (e.g. `https://example.com/path` → `example.com`). Invalid values are silently skipped. Maximum 100 values.

parameters.name: crmIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated record ids of companies in the CRM connected to the team (HubSpot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive); for Salesforce, the 18-character Account id. Returns the companies found in `data`, with `total` and no pagination, each with the matched id under `crmSync.crmRecordId`; ids that match nothing are skipped, and `data` is empty when no CRM is connected. Duplicates are removed; an empty value is ignored. Maximum 100 values (`TOO_MANY_CRM_IDS`); a value over 25 characters answers `INVALID_CRM_ID`. Ignored when `idsOrDomains` is provided.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of companies to skip for pagination. Defaults to 0. Ignored when `idsOrDomains` is provided.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description: The field by which to sort. Currently, only 'createdAt' is supported.

parameters.name: sortOrder
parameters.description: The sort direction. Use 'desc' for descending order; any other value (or omission) will sort in ascending order.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Search by company name (case insensitive)

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Returns selected fields. Returns all fields if empty. Each field is separated by a comma (e.g., '_id,fields.name,domain')

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of companies to retrieve. Default: 100. Maximum: 500

parameters.name: listId
parameters.description: Filter companies to the members of a CRM company list (`clt_xxx` format): a static list, or a dynamic list kept in sync with its filters. A legacy dynamic list, evaluated from its saved filters each time it is read, is rejected with `CRM_LIST_DYNAMIC`; both kinds of dynamic list show `dynamic: true` in `GET /companies/lists`. Combines with every other filter. Ignored when `idsOrDomains` is provided.

parameters.name: crmSyncStatus
parameters.description:
Filter companies by their CRM sync state against the team's active CRM provider. Requires a CRM (Hubspot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive) to be connected — otherwise the request returns `400 NO_CRM_CONNECTED`. Common values:
- `synced` — the company has a CRM record and no sync errors.
- `not_synced` — the company has no CRM record yet.
- `searching` — a CRM search (Search & connect, Create in CRM) is queued or running for the company.
- `not_found` — the last CRM search found no record for the company.
- `error` — at least one sync error is currently raised.
- A specific error reason (lowercase form), to filter by root cause: `unique_index_error_company`, `property_doesnt_exist`, `required_field_missing`, `company_already_exists_with_name`, `company_already_exists_with_linkedin_url`.

For each returned company, see `crmSync.errors[].metadata.alreadyExistingCompanyId` to identify the lemlist company that already occupies the conflicting CRM record (useful to remap contacts before deleting the duplicate).

parameters.name: fieldRejectionReason
parameters.description: Filter companies to those carrying a field rejection with this reason — a value lemlist refused to write, raised during CRM sync (`crm_sync_*`). Returns an empty list (`total: 0`) when no company matches. Each returned company exposes the full detail under `fieldRejections[]` (which field, why, and `conflictingRecordId` for duplicates). Independent of `crmSyncStatus` (which keys off the live provider errors); this filter reads the stored field rejections. Only applies to the paginated list — ignored when `idsOrDomains` is provided (that path returns the exact companies requested, unfiltered).

200.description: Success. Returns an object with `data` and `total`; `limit` and `offset` are only present on the paginated list, not with `idsOrDomains` or `crmIds`.

400.description: Either a plain `{ "error": "..." }` (`Bad team`, `limit` below 1), or a validation envelope. post.description:
Creates a new company or updates an existing one (upsert). If a company with the same domain, LinkedIn URL, or Sales Navigator URL already exists, it is updated as the `updateStrategy` query parameter says (by default, sent values replace stored ones and empty values are ignored). You can target an existing company directly by providing `companyId`, bypassing domain/LinkedIn matching, in which case `name` and the identifiers become optional. Without `companyId`, `name` is required together with at least one identifier: `domain`, `linkedinUrl` or `linkedinUrlSalesNav`.

**Permission:** creating a company requires the "Create companies" permission on the API key's user, otherwise the request fails with `403 COMPANY_CREATE_NOT_ALLOWED`. Updating an existing company does not.

domain.description: Company website domain (e.g. `lemlist.com`). Used as a unique key for upsert matching. Without `companyId`, at least one identifier is required among `domain`, `linkedinUrl` and `linkedinUrlSalesNav`. A personal email provider or a platform host (`gmail.com`, `facebook.com`, `linkedin.com`, a bare `wordpress.com`) is not stored: the company is written without it and `warnings` reports `COMPANY_DOMAIN_IGNORED`.

If the provided value does not match a team member, the company is still written with an `OWNER_NOT_FOUND` or `INVALID_OWNER_FORMAT` entry in `warnings`: the owner defaults to the API key owner on creation and is unchanged on update. On update it replaces the current owner, except under `fillEmptyOnly` where it is only set when the company has none.

source.description: Origin of the company record. Set on creation only and cannot be updated afterwards. Defaults to `api`.

Requires an admin API key. A new company is created already linked; an existing one has its link moved to this record, and its contacts’ associations follow. post.summary: Add or Remove Companies in a List
post.description:
Adds existing CRM companies to a static company list, or removes them when `?action=remove` is set.

- **Add** (default): send a `POST` with a `companyIds` body. Companies already in the list are silently skipped (no duplicates) and reported in `alreadyInList`.
- **Remove**: send a `POST` with `?action=remove` and a `companyIds` body. Companies that are not in the list are silently skipped; `removedCount` reflects the associations actually removed. This only affects list membership, the companies are not deleted from your CRM.

The list must be a **static** company list (`clt_xxx`). Dynamic lists (auto-populated by filter rules) and contact lists are rejected.

**Removal uses `POST ?action=remove` on purpose:** a `DELETE` request body is dropped by our stack, so `DELETE` on this path is **not supported** and returns `405 Method Not Allowed`.

post.description:
Merges up to 10 lemlist companies into one. The survivor (`primaryId`) keeps its id and every value it holds; its empty fields are filled from the other companies, which are then deleted. Everything attached to a deleted company (contacts, activities, tasks, list memberships) is moved to the survivor. When a CRM is connected, the survivor keeps its CRM link (or adopts the first linked record's when it has none) and receives the merged values there; lemlist never merges or deletes anything in the CRM itself, so the other records' CRM entries stay in the CRM, unlinked from lemlist — merge them CRM-side too, or a CRM import may recreate the duplicate.

The companies are folded into the survivor one at a time and the run **stops at the first failure**: `mergedIds` lists what went through, `remainingIds` what still exists. A first-fold failure returns an error instead — nothing was written.

**No undo:** deleted companies are gone.

primaryId.description: The surviving company. A lemlist company id (`cpn_xxx`).

secondaryIds.description: The companies folded into the survivor then deleted, 9 at most. A lemlist company id (`cpn_xxx`). Must not contain `primaryId`, and each company is listed once.

200.description: Merge run — **`success: true` does not mean complete.** The companies fold one at a time and the run stops at the first failure, so ALWAYS check `remainingIds`: the companies listed there were NOT merged and still exist. Fix the cause and call again with the survivor and the remaining ids.

primaryId.description: ID of the surviving lemlist company.

merged.description: `true` once at least one company was folded into the survivor.

mergedIds.description: IDs of the companies folded into the survivor and deleted, in fold order.

remainingIds.description: IDs of the companies NOT merged because an earlier fold failed. Empty when everything went through.

rejectedFields.description: Fields whose adopted value was refused by a uniqueness rule (kept survivor-side). Only present when it happened.

400.description: Invalid request. Possible error codes: `ENTITY_MERGE_INVALID_PAYLOAD` (missing `primaryId` or empty `secondaryIds`), `ENTITY_MERGE_SAME_ENTITY` (`primaryId` among `secondaryIds`, or a company listed twice), `ENTITY_MERGE_TOO_MANY_ENTITIES` (more than 9 `secondaryIds`).

post.summary: Search & Connect Companies in the CRM
post.description:
Searches your connected CRM for each company and links it to the CRM record found — the **Search & connect** action of the Companies page. No CRM record is ever created: use `POST /companies/crm/create` for that. Each company it links then syncs its mapped fields with that CRM record, which can update it.

Target the companies with `idsOrDomains` (lemlist ids or domains) **or** with `listId` for a whole company list: 10,000 companies at most either way, a domain counting every company that carries it.

**Asynchronous:** the call queues the work and answers at once with what was queued, not with what the CRM returned. Each company's outcome lands on its `crmSync` block shortly after: read it with `GET /companies?idsOrDomains=...` (100 per call), or, after a list, list its companies by state with `listId` and `crmSyncStatus`: `searching` while the search runs, then `synced` once linked, or `not_found` when no CRM record matched. Without `listId`, `crmSyncStatus` reads every company of the team: do not poll it.

- A company already linked to a CRM record is synced with it again (`alreadyLinked`).
- A company with nothing to search the CRM with is left untouched (`notSearchable`).
- A company whose CRM search is already queued is not queued twice (`alreadyInProgress`).

Requires a connected CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive, Attio or Zoho).

listId.description: A company list id (`clt_xxx`): acts on every company of the list, static or dynamic, 10,000 at most. Use it instead of `idsOrDomains`.

post.description:
Logs a call made outside lemlist, as an external dialer reports it. The call lands in the contact's timeline, the Calls table, the call stats and the connected CRM exactly like a call made with the lemlist dialer: a Call in HubSpot, a completed Task with its Call Result in Salesforce, a call activity in Pipedrive, following the **Calls** row of your activities mapping. Your outgoing webhooks fire as for any call.

**Who the call was with.** Send one of `taskId`, `leadId`, `contactId`, `email` or `phone`. A `taskId` (a call task of a campaign, from `GET /tasks`) completes that task with the call, so the campaign moves on as when a rep marks it done; the task's contact and lead are the call's, and a `contactId` or `leadId` sent alongside must agree with them. A `leadId` attaches the call to that lead and its campaign. The other three attach it to the contact alone: the call is logged, but the campaign automations of a call status (mark as interested, stop the campaign, pauses) need a lead, so pass `taskId` or `leadId` when the call belongs to a campaign.

**The numbers.** `from` is the caller's number and `to` the number called, international format: on an outbound call the rep's line and the contact's number, the reverse on an inbound one. They are written on the CRM call and shown in lemlist; the contact's side also finds the contact when none of the references above is sent.

**The rep.** `userId` is the lemlist user who made or took the call, a member of the team (`GET /team`): the call is attributed to them in the stats and owned by them in the CRM.

**The call status.** `callStatus` is a key of the team's statuses (`GET /call-statuses`). It runs the automations the team configured on that status, as when a rep picks it in the dialer. An unknown key is refused: lemlist never creates a status on the fly.

**Retries.** `externalId` is your own id of the call. Sending the same `externalId` again answers `200` with the stored call, unchanged, instead of logging it twice: retry freely on a network error. Two requests racing on one `externalId` answer `409 CALLS_API_LOG_IN_PROGRESS` to the second while the first writes the call, then `200` with the stored call; retry a `409` a moment later.

**Recording and transcript.** `recordingUrl` is fetched in the background and copied to lemlist's storage, so the call plays in lemlist after your link expires: send an `https` URL reachable from the public internet; `hasRecording` turns `true` once stored, and the CRM call note is refreshed with the recording link then. A plain-text `transcript` is stored with the call, feeds the AI call summary and the CRM call note. Both usually arrive after the call: send them later through `PATCH /calls/{id}`.

**Empty fields.** An optional field may be omitted or sent as `null`: both mean it is absent.

**Plan.** Email Pro and above, as `GET /activities`.

externalId.description: Your own id of the call, unique in your dialer. Letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `:` and `-`, 128 characters at most. The idempotency key: the same id never logs twice, and `PATCH /calls/{id}` accepts it.

userId.description: The lemlist user who made or took the call (`usr_…`), a member of the team.

from.description: The caller's number: the rep's line on an outbound call, the contact's number on an inbound one. Standardized to E.164 as the contact panel does (its own country code, else the team's billing country for a national number) and kept as sent otherwise: an anonymous caller, an extension or a test number that is no real number (`+15555555555`) never refuses the call. At most 32 characters.

to.description: The number called: the contact's number on an outbound call, the rep's line on an inbound one, standardized like `from`. On an outbound call its E.164 also finds the contact when no other reference is sent.

startedAt.description: When the call started, ISO 8601. May be in the past; at most 5 minutes in the future.

callStatus.description: A key of the team's call statuses (`GET /call-statuses`). Runs the automations that status carries, as the team configured them: lemlist's default statuses, `connected-positive` included, only count the call as answered; marking the lead interested or pausing its campaigns comes with a status the team set up so, read its `callPositive` and `pausesCampaigns` flags.

note.description: The rep's note on the call: shown with the call in lemlist and written in the CRM call note.
note.example: Asked for a demo next week.

recordingUrl.description: An `https` URL of the recording, reachable from the public internet. Fetched in the background. An empty string means no recording.

transcript.example: Hi Jane, this is Alex from lemlist…

provider.description: Your dialer's name, the same on every call you log. lemlist stores it lowercase, apart from `phoneProvider` (which stays `api`), to count calls by dialer. An empty string means none.

taskId.description: A call task of a campaign (`opp_…`, from `GET /tasks`): the call completes it and the sequence moves on. The task's contact and lead are the call's. To log a call on a lead without completing a task, send `leadId` or `contactId` instead.

leadId.description: The lead the call was with (`lea_…`), with its campaign.

contactId.description: The contact the call was with (`ctc_…`).

email.description: An email address of the contact the call was with.

phone.description: A phone number the call was with: the contact holding it in its phone field. Read as the contact panel reads a number: its own country code, else the team's billing country for a national number. A value that is no number names nobody (`CALLS_API_CONTACT_NOT_FOUND`).

patch.description:
Completes a call logged through `POST /calls` with what your dialer learns afterwards: the call status, a note, the duration, the recording, the transcript. Send at least one field; the others stay as they are. A field sent as `null` counts as absent.

`{id}` is the `_id` the log answered, or the `externalId` you sent. Only calls logged through the API are reachable: a call made with the lemlist dialer keeps its own media.

`callStatus` runs the status's automations as `POST /calls` does. `note` rewrites the call's note when one exists and creates it otherwise. `recordingUrl` and `transcript` behave as on `POST /calls`: the recording is fetched in the background, the transcript is stored and feeds the AI summary and the CRM call note.

**Plan.** Email Pro and above.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call's `_id` (`act_…`) or its `externalId`.

callStatus.description: A key of the team's call statuses (`GET /call-statuses`). Runs the automations that status carries, as the team configured them, and reaches the CRM call.

note.example: Left a voicemail, call back Thursday.

duration.description: Seconds. Moves the end of the call accordingly, and reaches the CRM call (HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive).

recordingUrl.description: An `https` URL of the recording, reachable from the public internet. An empty string means no recording, so it does not count as a field to update.

transcript.example: Hi Jane, this is Alex from lemlist…

post.description:
Start one enrichment for one person. Answers with the enrichment `id` right away; the result comes later through webhooks or [Get Enrichment Result](/api-reference/endpoints/enrich/get-enrichment-result). Every call starts a new enrichment and uses credits, even for a person enriched before.

Enable at least one of `findEmail`, `findPhone`, `verifyEmail` and `linkedinEnrichment`; a flag is on only when its value is the string `true`. Requesting `findEmail` and `verifyEmail` together runs only one of them: `verifyEmail` when a valid `email` is given, `findEmail` otherwise. Which inputs each workflow needs is listed in [Bulk Enrich Data](/api-reference/endpoints/enrich/bulk-enrich-data#required-inputs). Unknown or empty parameters are ignored.

post.description:
Creates a custom field on contacts or companies, or updates the one the entity already has under that `name`, under the rules of the lemlist app: the same reserved names, the same type conversions, the same permission.

**Create.** No field of that `name` on the entity: it is created, as the **New field** button does in the app. Any API key may create a field. The field is created on behalf of the user of the API key and logged in the team activity feed. Once created, write it through `POST /contacts` or `POST /companies` with its `name` as the key. A new contact field is then filled in the background from data lemlist already holds (the LinkedIn data of enriched contacts, the lead variable of the same name in your campaigns).

**Update.** A field of that `name` exists: the call updates it, and the API key user needs the **Update contact & companies fields** permission, as in the app (`403` otherwise, even when nothing would change). What can change:

- `label`, when sent and different;
- `type`, only to `text` or `multilineText`, from any type but `phone` and `user`: the conversions the app offers. The stored values are converted, as in the app. Any other `type` than the stored one answers `400 TYPE_CHANGE_NOT_ALLOWED`. Note that the app promotes a `text` field to `multilineText` on its own when a value with a line break reaches it (import, CRM, API), and `GET /fields` then lists it as `multilineText`: replaying a body with `type: "text"` converts it back and flattens the line breaks, as the app's **Change type** menu does;
- the options of a `select`, through `upsertOptions` (added when missing, never removed), `renameOptions` (the contacts or companies holding the old value are rewritten to the new one) and `removeOptions` (the contacts or companies holding the option are cleared). Applied in that order: renames, removals, additions. A select keeps at least one option. Options are matched as in the app, regardless of case and surrounding spaces: `gold` matches an existing `Gold`, renaming `Gold` to `GOLD` only changes its case, and values are stored without surrounding spaces, so a value written on a contact or company matches them. An operation already applied reads as done (a rename whose source is gone while its target exists, a removal of an absent option).

Sending the same body again changes nothing and answers `200` with empty `changes`.

Two calls changing the options of the same field at the same time: the one planned from a list that changed meanwhile answers `409 FIELD_CHANGED_RETRY` and writes nothing (the options are written first, before any `label` change); read the field again and replay the call.

**Name.** `name` is the key your integrations write to, and never changes afterwards: it must start with a lowercase letter, followed by letters and digits only. `label` is optional and defaults to `name` on creation.

**Synced with a CRM picklist (beta).** With `crmPicklist`, the call creates a `select` that mirrors a single-select picklist of your connected CRM, as the **Sync this picklist** switch does in the app: its options are the picklist's active options, kept in sync from then on, and the field is mapped to the CRM property both ways. Send `type: "select"` without option operations: the options come from the CRM. The team needs the beta (`403 BETA_NOT_ENABLED` otherwise), and the API key user the **Manage CRM settings** and **Edit integrations** permissions (`403 CRM_SYNC_PICKLIST_NOT_ALLOWED`). It only creates a field: a `name` already held by a field not synced with that very property answers `409 CRM_PICKLIST_FIELD_EXISTS` and changes nothing (an existing list is synced from the app, in your CRM settings > Field mapping, where you decide what each of its values becomes), while the same body sent again reads as an update of the field it created. The options of a synced field cannot be edited through the API (`409 FIELD_SYNCED_WITH_CRM`), and `GET /fields` lists it with its `crmPicklist`.

**Types.** `select` is created with its `upsertOptions` (at least one), or from a CRM picklist with `crmPicklist`. A `user` field takes a team member on `POST /contacts` or `POST /companies` (email or `usr_` id), as in the app.

**Read it back.** The response carries the field. A `GET /fields` sent right after may take a moment to list it. Renaming or removing an option, and converting a type, rewrite every contact or company of the team holding a value, within the call.

name.description: Key to write the field with on `POST /contacts` or `POST /companies`. Starts with a lowercase letter, followed by letters and digits only. Identifies the field to update; never changes afterwards.

type.description: Field data type. On an existing field, only `text` or `multilineText` may differ from the stored type (a conversion), and a `phone` or `user` field keeps its type.

label.description: Display name of the field, as shown in lemlist. Cannot contain an HTML tag (`<...>`). Optional: defaults to `name` on creation, unchanged when omitted on an update.

upsertOptions.description: Select fields only. On creation, the options (at least one). On an update, options to add when missing; the present ones and the others are kept, so the same list replays. Distinct and non-empty; compared as in the app, regardless of case and surrounding spaces (`gold` matches an existing `Gold`), and stored without surrounding spaces.

renameOptions.description: Select fields only, on an update: `{ "current value": "new value" }`. The option keeps its identity, so the contacts or companies holding the current value are rewritten to the new one.

removeOptions.description: Select fields only, on an update: options to drop. The contacts or companies holding one are cleared. At least one option must remain.

post.description:
Starts an AI contact-sourcing run for one or more accounts: sources each company's employees from the People Database and classifies them into a buying committee (decision maker / user / influencer) with an ICP fit score.

One account or two hundred, same call — pass a list of one.

Runs are asynchronous: the response carries a `runId` per account. Poll `GET /contact-sourcing` or subscribe to the `contactSourcingDone` webhook for the result.

The call answers `200` even when some accounts could not be started — one unrunnable account among 200 is not a reason to fail the rest. Read both `results` and `errors`.

By default an account that already has a committee is not re-run: its previous run comes back with `status: "reused"` and nothing is charged. `overwrite: true` forces a fresh run, but never stacks a second one on a run still going — that one is returned as `reused` instead, so retrying a timed-out request cannot charge you twice.

Takes lemlist company ids only. To start from a domain or LinkedIn URL, resolve it first with `GET /companies?idsOrDomains=`.

companyIds.description: Accounts to source contacts for (`cpn_xxx` format).

200.description: One entry per account, in the order they were given.

400.description: The body is not a non-empty list of company IDs, contains something other than a `cpn_` id, asks for more than 200 accounts, or `overwrite` is not a boolean.

403.description: The workspace does not have contact sourcing enabled.

422.description: The team has no AI Context set up, so there is nothing to judge fit against. In the lemlist app, open Settings > AI Context Center. Per-account problems — no website or LinkedIn URL, no credits, daily limit reached — are not this: they come back inside `errors`.

get.description:
Reads one contact-sourcing run — by its own id, or the latest run of an account.

The HTTP status carries the run state: `200` the run completed and `contacts` is filled, `202` the run is still queued or going (poll again), `400` the run failed and `error` says why, `404` no such run.

Exactly one of `runId` or `companyId` is required.

parameters.description: The run to read, as returned by `POST /contact-sourcing`.

parameters.name: companyId
parameters.description: Read the LATEST run of this account instead (`cpn_xxx` format).

400.description: The run failed; `error` says why.

404.description: No such run, or the account has never been sourced.

post.description:
Turns one contact-sourcing recommendation into a lemlist contact.

`leadId` comes from a run's `contacts[].leadId` — a People-Database id, not a contact id. `companyId` is required and verified: the new contact is filed under that account, whatever the person's profile lists as their current employer. Someone your workspace already has as a contact is left where they are — an Add never moves a contact from one account to another — and the call answers 409 rather than reporting a creation that did not happen.

patch.description:
Updates the `name` or `providers` of a waterfall. Only the fields present in the body change; `type` and `isDefault` cannot change, and `conditions` is rejected with a `400`.

When `providers` is sent it replaces the whole order; providers you leave out are appended, disabled. On a default waterfall this takes over from the lemlist order: `editor` becomes your user id and the list is followed as is; use the reset endpoint to hand it back to lemlist.

The full stored waterfall is returned.

400.description: Validation error. `code` is one of `ENRICHMENT_WATERFALL_INVALID_NAME`, `ENRICHMENT_WATERFALL_UNKNOWN_PROVIDER`, `ENRICHMENT_WATERFALL_DUPLICATE_PROVIDER`, `ENRICHMENT_WATERFALL_PROVIDER_NOT_CONNECTED`, `ENRICHMENT_WATERFALL_EMPTY_UPDATE`.

parameters.name: waterfallId
parameters.description: `default_email` or `default_phone`.

put.description:
Hands a default waterfall back to lemlist: `editor` becomes `lemlist` and the provider order is random again, as if nobody had ever edited it.

The reset waterfall is returned.

400.description: The waterfall is a custom one

example.error: Only default waterfalls can be reset
